#1953. Chichester City at home in play-off places – and glad to be at home at all

They had to dig in at Frome Town on Saturday – coming from a goal down to lead 3-1 then having to weather a late storm by the hosts.

Two more tough tests come in the next week – with Bath City visiting Oaklands Park on Saturday and City travelling to Chertsey on Tuesday. Bath and Chertsey are the two sides directly above Miles Rutherford’s City in the table.

Coach Darin Killpartrick said they were delighted to claim the points at Frome.

“Playing out as we like to do was difficult and we went with more pace up top in the second half. By the end we were hanging on. They threw the kitchen sink at us but we held on.”

Killpartrick said it was a great team effort but did single out double goalscorer Chebby for praise. The forward has scored six in his past six appearances and his Frome double came as a substitute.

Killpartrick said: “We’re seeing a lot of improvement in Brandon – he’s a terrific young man who is listening to us as coaches and working hard on his game, which is paying dividends.

“We’re still looking at what we feel his best position is, but he’s going to be an important player to us over the long season.”

Chi had no midweek match this week and Killpartrick said that was a blessing in a hectic spell in which free Tuesday nights were few and far between.

“It’s relentless and we are in a run where we have so many away games. We are currently in a run of seven away trips in ten games and for a small club, that is tough.”

With that in mind City will be glad to be back at home on Saturday to face high-flying Bath City. Killpartrick said: “We have had some fantastically entertaining home games this season, some brilliant football on show. We’d love a big crowd to come and get behind us.”

Curtis Da Costa and James Sweet are City’s main injury worries ahead of the weekend.

#1952. Arsenal vs Hull City - prediction, team news, lineups

By Ben Knapton | 05 Nov 2026 09:48, Last updated: 05 Nov 2026 10:17

Seeking to open a six-point lead at the top of the Premier League table - for at least a couple of hours - Arsenal host Hull City at the Emirates Stadium in Saturday's 3pm mismatch.

The Gunners' statement win over Liverpool put them back in control of their title destiny, whereas the Tigers' winless run continued in gameweek nine with a 2-2 draw against Ipswich Town.

Fourteen years this, 14 years that; every football fan and his dog was almost certainly aware of Arsenal's winless Premier League run at Anfield before the first ball was kicked last weekend, Mikel Arteta himself reminded plenty of the Gunners' sorry sequence without three points on Liverpool's turf.

However, having been a part of the hitherto last Arsenal squad to prevail in a top-flight match at Anfield, the Spaniard belatedly oversaw his first Premier League managerial victory away to Liverpool last weekend, when Kai Havertz's tap-in and a quintessential dogged defensive display downed Andoni Iraola's in-form crop.

If an Anfield success was not impressive enough for Arsenal, they managed it while denying Liverpool a single shot on target - according to some statistical suppliers - for the first time ever in a Premier League home game, albeit while counting their lucky stars that Jurrien Timber's seemingly blatant shirt pull on Alexander Isak in the box went unpunished.

Getting the rub of the green is a hallmark of champions, though, and Arsenal's triumph coupled with Manchester City's surprise home loss to Brighton & Hove Albion took the Gunners three points clear at the top; three can now become six, at least temporarily, as the Sky Blues kick off at 5.30pm on Saturday against Nottingham Forest.

Proving that their Brighton & Hove Albion battering was indeed just an anomaly, Arsenal are now on a four-game winning run in the Premier League, and their 24-point total after nine games is only bettered by the 2004-05 and 2007-08 teams (25 each) in the post-1992 era.

Furthermore, the holders are the only club with their 100% home record intact in the 2026-27 Premier League, and Wednesday's 2-1 Champions League success over Slavia Prague marked their third win from four in all tournaments.

Arsenal's three victories from their last four games matches Hull's total triumphs for the season, as since starting the campaign with a trio of successive wins in all tournaments, the Tigers have now either drawn or lost eight on the spin.

Sergej Jakirovic's side have suffered just two Premier League losses in that time - away to Newcastle United and Fulham - and have established a reputation as stalemate specialists, drawing a joint-high five games and sharing the spoils in three of their most recent four.

The Tigers were not terrific value for their 2-2 draw with Ipswich last weekend, though, enjoying just 39% of the ball and giving up four big chances to their fellow newly-promoted opponents, but a point was enough to consolidate their mid-table standing of 11th place.

Hull have now failed to keep a clean sheet in seven straight games in all tournaments, however, while also losing three of their last four games on the road in all tournaments, shipping six goals along the way.

The visitors' shock 2-1 Emirates success in 2008 remains one of their most famous results in history, but Arsenal have since strung together a 14-match unbeaten run against Hull, most recently triumphing 2-0 in February 2017 courtesy of an Alexis Sanchez double.

It was a case of one in, one out on the Arsenal defensive front on Wednesday, as while William Saliba made a matchday squad for the first time this season following a major back injury, Ezri Konsa was taken off just past the hour mark with an unexplained issue.

Konsa's status for Saturday is currently up in the air, but as Saliba was only an unused substitute against Slavia Prague, Cristhian Mosquera should be first in line to deputise for the former if need be.

Bukayo Saka (quad) and Max Dowman (suspended) are Arsenal's only confirmed absentees for the visit of Hull, which Viktor Gyokeres has done all he can to start after scoring one and setting up Noni Madueke in Prague.

However, the Swede is still expected to lose out to Kai Havertz, whose decisive goal at Anfield made him the highest-scoring German player in Premier League history.

On Hull's end, Jakirovic will have to cope without experienced midfielder Matt Crooks, who is suspended after picking up his fifth yellow card of the Premier League season against Ipswich.

Crooks joins Eliot Matazo (ACL), Matt Targett (ankle), Lucas Gourna-Douath (calf), Ilyas Ansah (back), Darko Gyabi (groin) and Charlie Hughes (groin) on the sidelines, but Jack Butland could return to the squad after an arm injury.

Unlike Crooks, first-choice striker Oli McBurnie avoided picking up a yellow against Ipswich which would have ruled him out of the Emirates trip, but the 30-year-old will miss the visit of Brighton & Hove Albion on November 22 if he is cautioned here.

Raya; Timber, Mosquera, Gabriel, Calafiori; Guimaraes, Rice; Madueke, Odegaard, Tzolis; Havertz

Tzolakis; Coyle, Egan, Mendy, Ajayi, Giles; Belloumi, Slater, Iroegbunam, Stroud; McBurnie

Hull in their 5-4-1 shape will do their utmost to frustrate Arsenal for as long as possible, but even a lightly fatigued Gunners side will find a way to break through eventually.

As the Tigers search for a response to no avail, Arteta's men should make the most of a more open contest, securing another straightforward win and extending their lead at the summit.

#1950. GdS: From a curse to a blessing – the factors behind Milan’s recent derby dominance

AC Milan won the derby again on Saturday night, continuing their recent dominance of the fixture, despite Inter celebrating more silverware.

La Gazzetta dello Sport write that Milan planted their flag in the middle of the Duomo and have not removed it for two years. Something strange is happening in the city, frankly inexplicable: Inter haven’t won in eight derbies, even though on paper they’re almost always the stronger team.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Since September 2024, the Nerazzurri have had eight matches against Milan, losing six and drawing too. But why does this keep happening? The paper have attempted to offer some explanations.

Between January 2023 and April 2024, Inter won six consecutive derbies. It became Stefano Pioli’s curse. Three matches were more difficult than the others: the two 2023 Champions League semi-finals and the April 2024 derby, in which Simone Inzaghi’s side sealed the Scudetto.

It was the pinnacle for Inter fans and the worst nightmare for Milan fans, not coincidentally commemorated last night by the Nord with its choreography. From that moment on, Milan turned things around.

In September 2024, they won with Matteo Gabbia’s 89th-minute header, and it all changed from there. A pair of draws, then the 3-0 Coppa Italia win with a Luka Jovic brace, the two 1-0 wins last season (Pulisic in the first leg, Estupinan in the return), and this 3-1 win most recently.

For the reasons, you should consult a psychologist, but some things can be understood. Milan certainly play much more freely than during those terrible 15 months.

They’re definitely finding tactical solutions they didn’t have in that run under Pioli, where they pressed hard and ended up only allowing counter-attacks. They especially struggled greatly against Dimarco, Calhanoglu, and Mkhitaryan.

Paulo Fonseca initiated the change, reinforced by Sergio Conceiçao in the Supercoppa Italiana final, by Massimiliano Allegri, and now by Amorim. Milan are increasingly confident and, as much as possible in a crazy situation like the derby, control the games.

This time, they struggled very little, even in the second half, as if they had the password to counter Inter’s moves. Much of it was a question of energy: Milan no longer fear their cousins, they go head-to-head, and often win the duels in recent derbies.

Then, of course, there are the individuals. Christian Pulisic is becoming a ghost for Inter, fitting of these times. CP11 has scored in four of the last eight derbies, and they’ve all been crucial goals. With his intelligence, he understands where to strike Inter. With his speed, he surprises them.

As for that intelligence thing, Luka Modric is second to none. In the derby that Pervis Estupinan won, he was the best on the field. In Saturday’s resounding win, he helped the team manage the tempo, defended up front, winning back valuable balls, and even left the free kick to Moreira.

Add Adrien Rabiot to the list of Inter nightmares: ‘the Duke’ has earned 7.5, 7, and 7.5 again in the three Milan derbies he has played (Gazzetta ratings). Throwing all that together, and you get a one-sided fixture.

#1948. Broadbridge Heath taste Sussex derby success – Horsham YM well-beaten by United

Broadbridge Heath 2-1 Crowborough Athletic

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

Broadbridge Heath welcomed Crowborough Athletic to the Air Engineering Stadium for this midweek clash between two former Southern Combination League clubs but it was Bears manager Chris Simmons’ side that picked up the points.

Crowborough came into the game on a run of four games unbeaten and they started on the front foot forcing a corner in the opening minutes which saw the ball come out to the lively Rushaar Samuel-Smikle who hit a right foot shot high and wide of target.

On 18 minutes George Hutcheon won the ball off a Heath defender wide on the right and played it inside to Harry Forster, who played it into the path of Findlay Chapman. He struck a fierce right foot shot from the edge of the penalty area that was saved brilliantly by Alfie Hadfield diving across to his left to push the ball out for a corner.

The half continued that way with the Crows pressing high up the pitch and preventing Simmons’ side from playing their free-flowing football and it was no real surprise when the visitors took the lead on 24 minutes.

Marcus Goldsmith won the ball wide on the right and just inside the Broadbridge Heath half, the Crows skipper played a long diagonal right foot cross into the penalty area to Harry Forster who leaped like a salmon to place a looping header over Hadfield and into the net.

On 30 minutes another Crows interception, this time by Hutceon, saw him win the ball wide on the right on the halfway line and playing it forward to Samuel-Smikle who advanced towards goal before he cut inside on to his left foot and hit a shot just wide of the far post.

With 5 minutes of the half remaining Forster received the ball in the middle of the park and played it forward to Goldsmith who then picked a pass to Samuel-Smikle who hammered a right foot shot just wide of the post and it remained 0-1 at the break.

Whatever was said in the Broadbridge Heath changing room at half-time certainly had an impact on the game with the Bears more lively, sharper and passing far more accurate than before.

They equalised on 64 minutes when Ben Royall received the ball in the left back position and drove forward before playing the ball to the feet of Sam Hards who played a pass between two defenders to allow Zac Jeanes to get away down the left flank.

The Heath forward took the ball to the goal-line before playing a pass across the face of goal to Charlie Connell in acres of space for a simple tap-in.

The game was changed completely within a minute of the restart when Sal Marino played a diagonal pass from the halfway line down the left channel to Jeanes who played it inside towards Sam Church. A defender intercepted the pass but only managed to play it straight to Sam Hards some 14 yards from goal who dispatched a low left foot shot that flew under the diving Charlie Holmwood to give the Bears the lead.

It was the fifth straight game that young Hards had got on the scoresheet.

The Bears continued to create chances with Lewis Hyde heading a Jeanes free kick just wide of the post, Zac Young trying a long range shot that was gathered comfortably by Holmwood and a goalmouth scramble saw the ball ping around the 6 yard box. But the game ended with a win for the Bears in what can best be described as the proverbial ‘game of two halves’.

Simmons said afterwards: “It was a really disappointing 1st half performance, they out worked and out fought us and our quality on the ball was poor, 2nd half was better, our equaliser was more like us and then Sam continued his great form with the winner.”

BBH: Hadfield, Richardson, Royall, Holden, Hyde (Salaam 77), Peters, Young (Rawlins 90), Church (Marino 70), Hards, Connell, Mann (Jeanes 60).

YM kept the visitors at bay for most of the first half, only to be overwhelmed in the second. In the slippery conditions an early sliding chance for Eastbourne went wide and although there were corners at each end, YM were getting limited possession and when it seemed inevitable that Eastbourne would score, Ryan Blunt duly obliged for them.

Amid two corners Eastbourne hit the post, but despite living dangerously, YM had done well to keep the deficit down to a single goal at the break.

As the second half progressed the gulf between the sides from opposite ends of the table became more apparent after an early second goal - with Blunt’s hat trick following in the 55th minute.

A rare YM chance was ballooned over ahead of Eastbourne’s fourth goal from Callum Barlow, just after the woodwork had spared YM.

Under constant pressure YM kept scrapping, and Eastbourne keeper Alieu Secka had to rush out to smother the ball – until, with little time left, sub Baran Kartel twisted the knife with the visitor’s fifth goal.

YM Joint Manager Alex Walsh told the County Times: "Eastbourne are a strong side and we never gave up but the quality isn’t there at the moment. We’ve got two potentially easier games coming up but we need to start getting the ball in the net.”

Thun doubled their lead in the 33rd minute through striker Brighton Labeau after more poor defending, this time from skipper Stephen Kingsley – who went off later with an injury – and then Furkan Dursun grabbed a third in the 56th minute before Jambos defender Stuart Findlay reduced the deficit in the 82nd minute with a header.

Hearts are left with one Conference League point out of nine following a 1-1 home draw against Nordsjaelland and a 2-0 defeat away to Trabzonspor.

Thick smoke from a pyro halted the game soon after kick-off but when play resumed after a lengthy delay – there were nine minutes added on at the end of the first half – Hearts winger Josh McPake drew a save from Niklas Steffen with an angled drive that lacked real power.

Thun’s second goal was also gift-wrapped.

The home side broke clear and with pace following a Heart set-piece and when Nils Reichmuth crossed into the box from the right, Kingsley stuck out a leg to clear but the ball went straight to Labeau who swept it into the net from 10 yards out.

Dursun was shown a yellow card for a forearm challenge into the face of Findlay, and it perhaps deserved more punishment.

The interval gave the Tynecastle side time to reset but three minutes after the break, Reus made a diving save from Dursun and an even better one from Reichmuth moments later. However, the keeper was beaten once again when Dursun got his toe to a Reichmuth cross.

On the hour mark, Nico Maier raced clear of the Hearts defence but although his chip beat Reus, it sped wide of the target.

The night got worse for the rattled visitors as injured Kingsley was replaced by 19-year-old debutant Matthew Gillies, called back from a loan spell at Stenhousemuir. Hearts were sporadic in their threat.

Malachi Fagan-Walcott’s header from a Jordi Altena free-kick was brilliantly saved by Steffen.

In the 78th minute Jan Bamert had the ball in the net after Steffen tipped a free-kick from substitute Nassim Zoukit on to the bar but was ruled offside, before Findlay headed in a consolation from another Altena free-kick.

#1944. Worthing FC puts focus on mental health as supporters association partners with suicide prevention charity Olly’s Future

The charity, founded by Worthing mum Ann Feloy, has been announced as Worthing FC Supporters Association's chosen charity of the year and a fundraising day was held on Saturday, October 31.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

Ann set up the charity in memory of her son Oliver Hare, who took his own life on February 14, 2017, just before his 23rd birthday. Its work includes delivering training worldwide to equip people with the skills to spot signs of someone who may be thinking of suicide and have a conversation that could help save their life.

Ann said: “We're delighted Worthing FC has chosen Olly's Future as its charity of the year. My son Oliver loved playing all kinds of sports, from football and rugby to tennis and squash.

“It's a local club being bold enough to get behind the message that suicide prevention is everyone's business, and particularly football where the majority of spectators are men.

“This is what the recent The Royal Foundation of the Prince and Princess of Wales' campaign On Your Side, hosted by Jake Mills Hub of Hope and fronted by Harry Kane, looks like on the ground.

“We all know the facts that three quarters of suicides are by men and that suicide is the biggest killer of men under 50. Supporting our suicide prevention charity goes a long way to reaching that vital target audience and we'll be working with the club to ensure we can help save lives from suicide together.

“However, this comes at a time when the town is in shock about the closure of its Worthing Samaritans branch, which has left volunteers reeling. I've spoken to many in the past week, since they were told of the closure of their premises in an efficiency drive.

“Local volunteers tell me they are being asked to work from home, which they feel is not tenable as it's vital for their own well-being to be with colleagues, or else drive to Brighton to carry out their shifts.

“For every step forward in suicide prevention, there seems to be two steps back. The Samaritans are closing numerous premises around the country - Worthing is not alone.”

The Rebels will be working with Olly’s Future throughout the coming season and the supporters association, run by Natalie Lunn, will be donating some of the proceeds from away match coach travel to the charity.

Natalie said: “I work as a nurse and know how difficult it is to access care for physical health let alone mental health. So when we were looking for a charity to support, I went online and found Olly’s Future, which is based locally.

“I have sons myself and some of their formative years were during Covid and I know how difficult it can be for young people. So,it is great to be able to contribute to a charity doing such valuable work.”

The club produced an enamel badge, linking the Love and Light logo of Olly’s Future with the team, for the fundraising day and this proved popular with supporters.

James Davies, Olly’s Future chief executive, has followed non-league football most of his life and he was part of the fundraising team on the day.

He said: “For us it is excellent to have such a relationship with a club which shows how much it cares about the issue of suicide.

“You see more than 3,000 people gathered together in one space and this offers a chance to open up about issues which are concerning them. They are with friends and are experiencing a sense of belonging as they get together to support the team.

“Non-league teams may not have the resources and the large fan-base of the bigger clubs, but they are very obviously rooted in towns such as Worthing and play a major part in the community. Tickets are also affordable in ways that premiership attendance is not for many people.”

His own recent personal experience has shown how much going to watch a match can mean to people who might otherwise be feeling isolated.

James explained: “I recently lost my grandmother and my grandfather, aged 87, had been her carer in her last years. He has started going each week to watch both Portland United and Weymouth matches along with other family members, which stops him just being at home and alone with his thoughts, and when I went with him, he really did open up about his feelings.”

It was feared that the former Celtic centre-back had suffered knee ligament damage following a challenge from Ebou Adams during Tuesday's 3-1 defeat at Portsmouth.

The 26-year-old immediately signalled to the Swansea coaching staff that he was unable to continue and was replaced by Benjamin Cabango with just 24 minutes on the clock.

#1942. Late push can’t save Lewes as Dartford win on fiery night at the Pan

In a clash of two high-flying teams in the Isthmian Premier Division table, a swift first-half double from Dartford proved decisive at The Dripping Pan.

Ben Greenhalgh’s powerful strike and Dan Smith’s opportune rebound punished two moments of Lewes disorganisation before the half hour. While the Rooks responded well, they struggled to break down a stubborn Darts backline and had to wait until the 82nd minute for a scorching Brian Garzon goal.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

Despite pouring everyone forward late on, this left too little time to secure an all-important equaliser.

Lewes began the evening with three changes to their starting XI, with Ben Mundele, Tyler Christian-Law and Danny Bassett returning in place of Tyler Cox, Kurtis Cumberbatch and Bobby Unwin.

After a spectacular entrance featuring Southover Bonfire Society’s torches and fireworks, the game itself proved more of a slow burner.

Both teams used the opening stages to feel one another out, and the first chance came after almost 15 minutes, when an unmarked Charlie Walker headed Danny Bassett’s delivery over the bar. Lewes then lost defender Harry Mills to an awkward injury, forcing them into a reshuffle as Olly Hamstead came on.

Just a minute later, Dartford seized upon this as player-manager Greenhalgh found space on the edge of the box for a sharp left-footed strike into the top left corner. The Rooks were almost immediately level when Mundele connected with Christian-Law in the box, but the midfielder couldn’t get a clean connection on his effort.

Heading back up the other end, Dartford then doubled their advantage as an initial shot was saved by Louis Rogers and the Lewes defence was too slow to react as Smith drilled home. The Rooks stabilised and began to gather some momentum before half-time.

Their best chance came as Ryan Gondoh drove forward and found Charlie Walker, who in turn located Garzon for a powerful drive stopped by defender Ben Swift. After what was surely a frank discussion at the break, Lewes returned with much more of the ball in the second half.

Dartford proved a tough nut to crack, with their fluid system quick to close down any gaps and continuing to threaten on the counter. Charlie Walker won a free-kick 20 yards from goal in the 55th minute but sent the set piece over the crossbar.

This spell proved Lewes needed a change of system, and with Tyler Cox replacing Mundele, the Rooks soon moved to a back three. It did the trick of freeing up Cox and Jack Enkh, who posed regular problems for the visiting defence.

With Bassett and Walker also taken off, the Rooks opted for a system featuring multiple runners but no clear central target. Chances started to flow at both ends, with Enkh crashing a shot into the side-netting, Garzon having an effort saved by Ryan Sandford and Hamstead clearing the danger at the other end as Max Fiddes went clean through.

Gondoh was then foiled by Sandford as his shot took a deflection off George Whitefield.

In the 82nd minute, Lewes found their breakthrough as Gondoh drove down the right and found Garzon on the edge of the box, where he fizzed a low shot past Sandford. The Rooks pushed hard in the remaining minutes, but Dartford dropped deep and closed off any angles towards goal.

The best remaining chance fell to Tyrese Owen in an added-time pinball in the box, as his audacious backheel was hooked away. Lewes therefore tasted defeat at home for just the second time this season, while a five-match unbeaten run in October came to an end.

The Rooks are 4th in the table after 15 games and now head to 12th-placed Dulwich Hamlet this weekend. Kick-off is 3pm at Champion Hill on Saturday.

Lewes FC: Rogers; Mundele (Cox, 63’), Mills (Hamstead, 21’), Spinks, Enkh; Christian-Law, Owen; Gondoh, Garzon, Bassett (Fisher, 70’); Walker (Unwin, 72’)

#1941. PSG make January window decision after Khvicha Kvaratskhelia injury

By Axel Clody | 05 Nov 2026 10:06

Following the serious injury to Khvicha Kvaratskhelia, Paris Saint-Germain have made their choice between signing a winger in the January transfer window or trusting their current squad.

On 20 October, Khvicha Kvaratskhelia went off injured in the 4-2 win over Barcelona. The Georgian suffered a rupture of the anterior cruciate ligament in his right knee. It is a heavy blow for the former Napoli player, who could miss the rest of the season, and for Paris Saint-Germain, who will have to do without a key part of their attack for many months.

Faced with Kvaratskhelia’s long absence, Paris appeared to have three options to replace their star: move Desire Doue to the left, trust summer signing Mika Godts or look for a left winger this winter. After several weeks of reflection, Paris Saint-Germain have made their decision.

According to Canal+ journalist Olivier Tallaron, the capital club will not sign any player to replace their left winger in the next winter transfer window, unless another important member of the Parisian attack suffers a significant injury.

Although the same source did not specify the reasons for this choice, Luis Enrique and his staff appear satisfied with their current squad despite this heavy absence. Desire Doue has performed in the left-wing position, as has Mika Godts, since Kvaratskhelia’s injury.

The Spaniard also relies on a squad that is strong in both quality and quantity, and on versatile players.

Homegrown midfielder Senny Mayulu is currently shining as a false number nine. Right winger Maghnes Akliouche is gaining importance and can also play up front or in midfield.

This season, goalscorer Ferran Torres has also played on occasion as a right winger and on the left side. It was in that latter position that he scored a hat-trick against Slovan Bratislava (6-1). Paris therefore have what they need to keep performing without Kvaratskhelia.

Paris Saint-Germain, who are in outstanding form at the moment even with Ousmane Dembele also in the treatment room, have chosen to trust their current attacking department.

Kvaratskhelia’s absence will notably allow the two summer signings, Mika Godts and Maghnes Akliouche, to gain more playing time, assimilate Luis Enrique’s principles more quickly and continue their progress.

#1940. Florenzi reveals what Maignan and Bartesaghi told him after ‘needed’ derby win

Alessandro Florenzi has revealed that he spoke to two of his former team-mates after the derby win over Inter.

It was a big win for AC Milan on Saturday night at San Siro as they bounced back from the defeat to Bologna in the best possible way, scoring three times in the first half to overcome their city rivals for the fourth straight time.

The win left Gerry Cardinale feeling emotional, such was the magnitude. Diego Moreira was the start of the show with a goal and two assists, but everyone to a man put in a serious shift to ensure an eighth straight derby without defeat.

Florenzi was part of the Sky panel that covered the match at San Siro, and he revealed that he had a conversation with two players in the current squad as they headed off at full-time. His words are via Goal.

“I spoke to Maignan and Bartesaghi before they went back into the tunnel. They were happy and made it clear to me that they needed this win. They needed it for their morale, to keep going on a path that isn’t easy,” he said.

“The Milan side we saw tonight certainly give cause for optimism and, as they were also saying in the studio, Rabiot and Pulisic are, for me, the leaders on the pitch whom Milan struggle to do without. Moreira also had an outstanding game.”

#1939. Savio scores on debut as Spurs cruise past Charlton in Carabao Cup

It looked like this was going to be a night for “one of their own”, but Tottenham Hotspur’s latest big-money arrival, Sávio, stole the headlines to crank up the excitement at his new club.

Mikey Moore had set Spurs on their way to what proved a comfortable Carabao Cup success over Championship club Charlton Athletic and heard his name sung by the home fans.

But Sávio stepped off the substitutes’ bench to take the limelight with a late goal just a few days after completing his expensive switch from Manchester City, and head coach Roberto De Zerbi is demanding many more to come.

“A perfect day for him,” said De Zerbi. “His biggest improvement is to increase the number of goals. He is one of the best wingers, but the best wingers score many goals and I spoke with him two days ago, and we put the goal at 10-12 goals.

“We need 10-12 goals from the wingers. Last season, we suffered too much because the number of goals were not enough.”

"What an introduction!"Sávio scores a brilliant goal on his Spurs debut! 👏 pic.twitter.com/WgmcfgeNpX

Having watched some of Tottenham’s signings fall to a 3-0 Premier League defeat by Brentford a few days earlier, Sávio’s late impact was the perfect lift for the Spurs supporters.

The club have committed to spending almost £400m this summer, leading to debate by outsiders over whether it will prove to be money well spent and huge waves of excitement within the fanbase.

A deal that could be worth as much as £85m, if add-ons are achieved, for Sávio certainly raised some eyebrows, but the Brazilian provided the perfect response by scoring just 11 minutes into his debut as a late substitute.

In the 82nd minute, Sávio cut in from the flank and scored with a shot past Charlton goalkeeper Tiernan Brooks. He and the Spurs crowd thought he had a second a few minutes later, but his shot hit Ben Davies on its way into the net and the defender was credited with the goal.

Having sung for Moore earlier in the game, the Spurs fans wasted no time in trying out their new song for Sávio, inspired by the Spandau Ballet hit Gold.

Moore has been expected to move to Cologne on loan, but provided a reminder of his talent by opening the scoring in the first half with only his second goal for the club.

What a hit from Mikey Moore! ⚪ pic.twitter.com/OgSM4qhiqs

“We have to understand the best solution,” De Zerbi said. “I would like to keep him. He’s young but a good player, but we can’t make the wrong decision. He needs to play, he needs to get games inside him.”

Cutting in from the right, where Sávio is primed to play, Moore surged past his marker and shot from just inside the box. Brooks should have stopped it, but the ball flew past him and into the net.

Three minutes after Moore’s opener, Dominic Solanke scored his first goal since March to offer a reminder of what he can still give De Zerbi, who is poised to welcome Omar Marmoush to Tottenham.

Buoyed by his first-half goal, Moore skipped his way around a couple of tackles at the start of the second period but his low cross was cut out. The Spurs fans responded by singing “he’s one of our own.”

Substitute Kevin Danso netted with his first touch from a header, before Sávio was introduced to steal the show, despite a late consolation goal from Charlton’s Lloyd Jones.

Kevin Danso scores with his first touch since coming on! ⚪ pic.twitter.com/oqUU7wjoJW

The victory set up a tough third-round trip to Anfield to face Liverpool for Tottenham, but De Zerbi said: “It’s a great game. If we want to win the competition we have to win the games.

“Sometimes in this competition, it can happen that you play against big teams. It’s a great challenge for the players, for me, for our clubs. We have to arrive ready to play in our style, with personality, ready to play a game following the work we are doing on the training ground.”

The last competitive meeting between these sides came in the FA Cup back in January 2011, with Tottenham winning that game 3-0 at White Hart Lane. A then 19-year-old Andros Townsend made his debut that day and scored, with Jermain Defoe scoring a brace.

Tottenham’s Premier League campaign got off to the worst possible start as they lost 3-0 at Brentford last weekend. Tottenham have been very busy during this summer transfer window and that has continued this week. Savio (formerly Savinho) has arrived from Manchester City in a deal that could be worth £85m and the Brazilian could make his Tottenham debut tonight, having been registered in time.

“I think in attacking positions we need players capable one-on one, to create something, to create a chance to score,” Roberto De Zerbi said. “In terms of one-on-one, he [Savio] is one of the best players, especially since 2024. He can play on the right side, on the left side. I have known him from a long time, I spoke with him when he went to Manchester City. He is a big player for us.

“I do not know if I am the right man [to get the most out of Savio], but for sure he has to achieve. I think a player who is so good in one-on-one, so good at creating chances to score, to be complete, he has to score. If you analyse the other best wingers in the world, many of them, they score 10 to 15 goals per season. He has the qualities. Maybe his habits, he has to change habits, because he has to be focused on the assists, the one-on-one dribbling and also to score.”

Omar Marmoush is closing in on an initial loan deal from Manchester City but that move is not complete and thus he is not available for Tottenham tonight. Micky van der Ven and Pedro Porro are both available having missed Tottenham’s loss at Brentford but the hosts are still without Xavi Simons, Pape Sarr, Dejan Kulusevski and Wilson Odobert.

Charlton have made the perfect start to their Championship campaign; a 2-1 home win over Derby was followed up by a 2-1 victory at recently-relegated West Ham. Nathan Jones’ side earned their place in the League Cup second round with a 3-1 win at Cheltenham in the first round.

“We have to be very organised and very professional, they [Tottenham] are a top team,” Jones said. “They have a great manager and a brilliant group of players. They already had a Premier League squad and they have spent, what is reaching about, I do not know, £300 million or something like that. It is a wonderful test, we have to be right near our best and do both sides of the game very well. Of course, you want to test yourself against the best managers and you want to test yourself against the best teams. For us, this is not our priority, the Championship is our priority, but this is the next game and therefore it is the most important.”

#1938. Wouter Vrancken's Hearts message after Swiss setback - 'we have to stick together'

Wouter Vrancken insists Hearts will have to stick together following their self-inflicted 3-1 Conference League defeat by Thun in Switzerland.

The Scottish outfit, without 10 players through various injuries, fell behind in the 22nd minute when defender Jamie McCart knocked the ball into his own net.

Did you know with a Digital Subscription to The Scotsman, you can get unlimited access to the website including our premium content, as well as benefiting from fewer ads, loyalty rewards and much more.

Thun doubled their lead in the 33rd minute through striker Brighton Labeau after a poor attempted clearance from captain Stephen Kingsley – who went off later with an injury – and then Furkan Dursun grabbed a third in the 56th minute.

Jambos defender Stuart Findlay then gave some unrealised hope of a comeback in the 82nd minute when he headed in from close range.

After three Conference League fixtures Hearts have one point out of nine and have won just two of their last 10 fixtures in all competitions.

Vrancken told TNT Sports: “Like I said already to the guys, we have to stick together now. We know which situation we’re in with all the circumstances.

“And there’s only one thing that you have to do now and that is stick together and keep working hard. In general, it was not good enough in quality and can you blame them?

“Yeah, on one hand you can because you want to always expect the best and want the best. On the other hand, I’m still proud of what they did already in the run-up games.”

Kingsley was replaced in the second half by 19-year-old Matthew Gillies, called back from a loan spell at Stenhousemuir amid the club’s injury crisis, and Vrancken admitted there was an element of risk playing him on the artificial surface which the Jambos boss had criticised.

He said: “We talked it through before the game of course, a few days before the game. And yeah, it’s always a risk, especially when it’s another surface, and especially when it’s bad like that, but he was confident in playing and that’s where we are.”

Hearts’ next Conference League game is against Ligue 1 side in Monaco at Tynecastle on November 26 but Vrancken is more concerned about the home William Hill Premiership game against Falkirk on Sunday.

He said: “Monaco’s a really strong side, maybe the strongest side we will face in Europe. So we will see when we get there, because I think there are a lot of important games before that, especially on Sunday.”

#1937. Horsham FC boss hails biggest National League South victory to date – but cup win is forgettable

The ruthless Hornets served up a Halloween treat for their supporters as they stormed to a 5-0 win at Farnborough on Saturday.

The visitors led 2-0 at half-time through James Hammond’s free kick and Greg Luer’s tidy finish. George Cox’s rocket, Reece Myles-Meekums’ close-range effort and Harvey Sparks’ ferocious strike sealed Horsham’s biggest step two win in the second half.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

The thumping victory moved the Hornets up to tenth – and within three points of the play-off places – going into this Saturday’s home clash with AFC Totton.

Di Paola told us: “We’ve had a Jekyll & Hyde week really, but Saturday was brilliant. We played really, really well. There were some excellent goals and it was a brilliant performance.

“Even when they put us under the cosh at times, we defended really well and looked like a good unit. Collectively there were some really good performances.

“It was a much-needed win against one of the teams near us. It’s amazing because if you get the second or third goal, with the way we play, then the game becomes quite easy. What’s been the challenge in this league, and will continue to be the challenge, is getting those second or third goals to take the game away from the opposition.

“We had such good support on Saturday. It’s such a nice thing when you have a good performance and that level of support. I could see how happy they were.”

Horsham went ahead at Farnborough in the 43rd minute courtesy of a delicious Hammond free-kick. Luer then added the Hornets’ second on the stroke of half-time after good work from Charlie Hester-Cook to win the ball deep in Farnborough territory.

Cox made it three with a ferocious 25-yard piledriver on 74 minutes before Myles-Meekums poked home from close-range for Horsham’s fourth four minutes later.

Substitute Sparks then added the icing on the cake in second half stoppage time to confirm the Hornets’ biggest ever National League South win.

And Di Paola revealed Sparks’ goal was his pick of the bunch.

He added: “Harvey’s was my favourite just because of the way we pulled them all over the pitch and then attacked the space. That’s the kind of thing you look at and work on in training.

“It doesn’t always happen like that. It was nice to pull them all the way back into our half, go all the way back through the pitch, come outside where we’ve created space and go and score. It was a good way to win the game.

“The bundled goal was a bit different, but it was a good day at the office really.”

But Horsham were far less fluent away to SCFL Premier outfit Pagham in the Sussex Senior Cup on Tuesday evening.

A heavily-rotated Hornets team left it late to edge past the Lions 1-0, Ashley Nadesan tapping home with just three minutes remaining after Pagham’s goalkeeper dropped a high-hanging cross at his feet.

Di Paola said: “The highlight for me was that the game finished. It was an awful game of football played on an awful pitch.

“The pitch levelled the game, which meant we couldn’t play any real football. That’s not an insult to Pagham. When I was at East Preston, me and another guy used to jump on the mower and try and make the pitch as nice as possible back in the day. At Climping, when it got to October and the pitch was like a cow field. I’m not being a snob, I just think it’s very difficult to do anything on a bad pitch.

“There were a fair few performances that I was really unhappy with – and I said that to the boys at half-time. I thought some of them were bad – not because we haven’t gone and rattled 20 past them, but because of the general application and lack of desire.

“We mixed and matched it. You have to demonstrate why you’re not playing. It doesn’t mean you have to play well, you need to have the right attitude.

“People don’t need to impress me with goals or unbelievable play, I want players to give everything. I felt in the first half, in particular, we were slow in everything we did. We didn’t press, we didn’t sprint, we played within ourselves.

“A few didn’t do themselves any favours in the first half. In the second, we were slightly better. I thought Niall McManus was good, I thought Jack Brivio had a good second half, but not many of them came out with a great deal of credit.

“I’m glad we got through and got a goal late on. It was a tough night, frustrating night, an awful game of football. Anyone who came to watch that just didn’t see any real quality in the whole game.”

The victory at Pagham was Di Paola’s 300th as Horsham manager – but the boss was ambivalent about the milestone.

He added: “When I get to 1,000 games I will be quite proud of that one. I think that could be next season if we carry on, which I think is quite an achievement – but those kinds of milestones don’t really mean anything to be honest. I didn’t know anything about it.

“But that’s 300 good days in 12 years. We’ve almost got a year of good days!

“I personally don’t really look at stuff like that. It doesn’t make a lot of difference to me. When we get to the 1,000th game I will crack open a cider and wonder what I’ve done with my life!”

The Hornets have no fresh injury concerns ahead of Saturday’s home encounter with 18th-placed AFC Totton.

#1936. Celtic player ratings v Besiktas: game-changers produce late fireworks as trio of starters struggle

Marks out of ten for Celtic players after crucial 3-2 victory on matchday four of the Europa League

There were fireworks aplenty at Celtic Park on Bonfire Night as Martin O’Neill’s side produced a stunning late turnaround to claim a dramatic 3-2 victory over Besiktas and finally get their Europa League campaign up and running.

For long spells, this looked destined to be another miserable European evening for the Scottish champions. An uninspiring first-half performance was followed by Jordan Lotomba’s penalty concession and Junior Olaitan’s opener, leaving the Hoops staring down the barrel of a fourth consecutive league phase defeat.

However, the second-half introduction of Callum Osmand and Camilo Duran changed the complexion of the contest, with the substitutes turning a seemingly lost cause into a memorable comeback victory.

Osmand equalised before Duran struck twice in quick succession, including an 87th-minute winner, after Orkun Kokcu had threatened to spoil the party with a ferocious long-range effort.

It was a result Celtic desperately craved. Their European campaign had been in danger of unravelling after three successive defeats, following on from their failure to negotiate Champions League qualification against LASK. O’Neill had previously insisted there should be no ceiling on his side's continental ambitions, but with the games beginning to run out, this was effectively a must-win encounter.

Besiktas arrived in Glasgow in considerably better shape, sitting eighth in the 36-team standings after wins over Marseille and Hoffenheim and a draw with Crystal Palace. Celtic, meanwhile, were looking to avoid four consecutive losses in major European competition for the first time since December 2017.

There were familiar faces in the visiting ranks, too. Vaclav Cerny returned to the east end of Glasgow following his controversial water-bottle incident involving Celtic supporters during Rangers’ 3-2 victory in March last year. Former Hoops striker Oh Hyeon-gyu also featured, while ex-Rangers defender Ridvan Yilmaz was named among the substitutes.

Firework displays offered some pre-match spectacle outside the stadium, but the atmosphere inside was subdued, with a sparse home crowd reflecting the growing discontent surrounding the club.

The opening exchanges offered little to lift the mood. Celtic struggled to build any real momentum, with the loudest reaction from the home support coming whenever Cerny found himself in possession.

The visitors gradually assumed control as Celtic struggled to keep hold of the ball. By the 39th minute, the home side had registered just two touches inside the opposition penalty area. Nygren's air shot inside the Besiktas box shortly before the interval summarised Celtic's attacking frustrations.

Their evening took a turn for the worse in the 52nd minute. Jordan Lotomba, on his first start at right-back, made a rash sliding challenge on Ernest Poku right on the edge of the penalty area, with the contact occurring on the line. The referee had little hesitation in pointing to the spot.

Sam Johnstone initially produced an one-handed save to deny Olaitan, but the goalkeeper was left helpless as the Besiktas forward reacted quickest to convert the rebound.

At that stage, Celtic looked short of ideas and confidence, with the prospect of a fourth straight European defeat looming large.

Then came the turning point. O’Neill introduced Osmand, and the youngster needed just 43 seconds to make his mark. Callum McGregor threaded a delightful reverse pass into his path, allowing the 20-year-old to take one touch before drilling a composed finish into the bottom corner.

The goal sparked an immediate transformation. Celtic suddenly had purpose and aggression, with the crowd responding to the renewed energy on the pitch. Lia Scales went close to levelling matters when his deflected header was superbly clawed over the crossbar by Alexander Nubel, while Nygren dragged another opportunity narrowly wide after being picked out by Osmand.

Celtic's second goal felt increasingly inevitable. It arrived in the 78th minute, with Duran providing the finishing touch to another superb attacking move. Having been shifted into the central striking position, the Colombian immediately demonstrated what he could offer through the middle, timing his run perfectly to latch onto Osmand's pass, carrying the ball round Nubel and slotting into the unguarded net.

The hosts looked capable of adding to their tally in the closing stages, but Besiktas had one final response. Kokcu, introduced from the bench, unleashed a sublime effort from around 25 yards that flew into the bottom-left corner, leaving Johnstone with no chance.

It was a devastating blow so late in the contest, but Celtic were not finished. Just two minutes later, Duran once again found space behind the visitors defence as Tierney's effort fell invitingly into his path. The striker displayed clever footwork to bring the ball under control before stabbing it beyond Nubel to restore Celtic's lead.

This time, there would be no way back for the visitors. There is still plenty of ground to make up in the Europa League standings, but Celtic have at least given themselves something to build on with this result.

We give each player a mark out of ten for their display.

Kept his place despite conceding five goals in his previous three domestic games. Produced an excellent first-half save to tip Trossard’s ferocious, albeit offside, strike on to the crossbar. Strong right hand to keep out Olaitan’s penalty but couldn’t prevent the rebound. No chance of getting to Kokcu's 25-yard wonder strike. 6 | SNS Group

Making his first start since arriving from Feyenoord in the summer, he struggled to cope with the Turks’ threat down his side, often being dragged out of position. A clumsy tackle on Poku resulted in the penalty award. Looked to make amends with a lung-busting run from his own half to the edge of the box, but unable to get a shot away. Withdrawn shortly after. 4 | PA

The ever-dependable American was rock solid throughout. Made an important early intervention to deny Trossard and produced arguably one of his best performances so far this season. Subbed late on. 7 | SNS Group

A sliding challenge prevented Cerny from testing the keeper early on. Lapse in concentration almost proved costly as Besiktas threatened midway through the first half. Fortunate to escape a booking for a shirt pull on Oh. Saw a deflected second-half header require a sharp save to claw it over the bar. 6 | SNS Group

#1934. Heartbreak for 10 men Roffey: Roffey 1 – 2 East Grinstead

Roffey welcomed East Grinstead to the Fusion Aviation stadium for this clash between two of the Premier’s promotion chasers. The night started so well for the Boars but ended in disappointment after Callum Chesworth was controversially sent off, leaving them to play seventy minutes with ten men.

After three minutes a Luke Harrison throw in found Jordan Mase in the penalty area. The Boars skipper found Chesworth who cut the ball back for Callum Kilkenny to sweep the ball inside the far post for an early lead. Roffey were quickly into their passing rhythm, breaking up Grinstead attacks and playing their way up the field confidently. After seven minutes a short corner routine ended Byron Napper’s shot being blocked for another corner as the visitors were pushed back.

Did you know with an ad-lite subscription to SussexWorld, you get 70% fewer ads while viewing the news that matters to you.

Grinstead came close on eleven minutes when Kieron Pamment got down the left and fired a shot across goal just missing the far post. Ex Hornet Charlie Harris attempted a ‘Diego Gomez’ long shot when he saw Monty Watson-Price, deputising for Charlie Burton who was playing for Bromley in the FA Youth Cup, off his line. His effort however cleared the bar. At the other end, a free kick was worked to Bailey Moyo who got past his marker, but his cross could only find Harry Howes in the Wasps’ goal.

Roffey’s high press was keeping Grinstead in most of the time but Watson Price had to be quick out of his area to block Pamment’s run when he had been beaten the offside. Grinstead regained possession and the ball was played into the area where Napper, under pressure from Dan Cole, deflected the ball over Watson-Price and into the net. The Wasp’s joy was short lived as the linesman decided that Cole was offside when the ball was played into the box.

Then came the key moment in the game. Chesworth turned away from his marker but the ball ran away from him and he put in a challenge to win it back which he appeared to have done but in doing so made contact with an opponent and the referee blew for the kick, told the Roffey striker that it was never a red card and took out his yellow. Then for some reason he changed his mind and to the surprise of most people in the ground, showed a red card.

So, with seventy minutes left, Roffey had to face one of the best teams in the league with a man less. How would they adapt? The answer was soon apparent, they continued in virtually the same manner with Mase and others getting forward to fill the gap that Chesworth’s departure had left. They continued they’re passing game, but Grinstead now had added momentum and Jack Meeres blocked a shot for a corner which after a couple of headers, ended up in Watson-Price’s arms. The Roffey stopper then had to go down sharply to his left to keep out a shot from Starkey with Meeres tidying up the rebound.

As half time approached Roffey continued to have the most possession, Mase and Gibson had shots blocked and after a long spell of possession around the Wasp’s penalty area, Howes saved Pat Gibbs drive. Watson-Price comfortably took a shot from Harris. Roffey were still getting forward earning corners and putting pressure on the visitors and when Grinstead threatened through Pamment and Cascoe Rogers, Meeres and Gibbs repelled everything coming into the box. Half time arrived with the balance of the game the same as when it had been 11v11.

Roffey started the second half with the same ten and showed no sign of sitting back and holding on. Callum Kilkenny was replaced by Evan Hoarty on fifty minutes after a knock but this made no difference to the Boars approach. Gibbs headed away when Perry looked like he was going into get onto a cross 8 yards out.

Roffey were getting forward in numbers and when Mase got to the byline and pulled the ball back, it was right back, Luke Harrison he found, unfortunately Harrison’s shot missed the far post by inches. Mase again got behind the defence, this time finding Moyo whose shot could not beat Howes. A third chance to get the important second goal came when Hoarty weaved his way into a shooting position but could not get the contact he would have wanted with the shot which was again saved by Howes.

As often seems to happen a missed chance at one end is followed by a goal at the other. Cooper headed wide from a corner then for the first time Pamment found some space in the Boars defence and finished clinically for the equaliser. Tom Caplin came on for Bailey Moyo and as we entered the last ten minutes, Teddy Wood, who had covered every blade of 3G grass was replaced by Max Mesquita. Both teams were still in the hunt for the three points with Omar Folkes adding to the Grinstead forward line but as we entered stoppage time, maybe fatigue finally got the Boars who couldn’t clear a corner and after a scramble it was Folkes who managed to force it home. Cue wild celebrations from the visitors and their bench.

Roffey pinned Grinstead in their half for the last three minutes but couldn’t find the final touch to get an equaliser. They did get the ball in the net but it was ruled out for offside. It had been great effort with ten men for most of the game but looking back the Boars will know they had created the chances to win the game. Small margins count in the end and although they received great compliments from the opposition and their supporters the young Boars were left with a feeling of frustration. They will have a chance to get back on the winning trail on Saturday at Little Common.

Roffey: Watson-Price, Harrison, Gibson, Napper, Gibbs, Meeres, Wood(Mesquita), Mase, Chesworth, Kilkenny(Hoarty), Moyo(Caplin) Subs: Allen, Berry.

#1933. Celtic cure insomnia before subs make the difference to spark Europa League lift-off

Goals from the bench as Celtic come from behind to claim 3-2 win over Besiktas

Celtic are up and running in the Europa League at the fourth time of asking after a crucial 3-2 home win over Besiktas.

After losing their opening three games, Celtic needed a positive result against the Turkish side and showed fortitude to come back from a goal down to breathe life into their aspirations of reaching the knock-out stages.

They were thankful for supersubs Callum Osmand and Camilo Duran, who came on to rescue the match for Celtic in an action-packed second half following Besiktas' 54th-minute opener. The win leaves Celtic in 32nd place with three points at the halfway stage of the main phase.

Celtic travel to Torreense of Portugal and Cypriot outfit Omonia later this year before matches against Marseille (home) and Union (away) in January. They can head into those fixtures with some optimism after a much-needed victory, only their fourth in 11 matches across all competitions.

Manager Martin O'Neill came into this match under pressure following Sunday's 2-0 defeat by Falkirk. The 74-year-old rotated his team, giving rare starts to right-back Jordan Lotomba and winger James Forrest, and introduced his key players at the right time.

The first half could have been bottled up and used as an insomnia cure. Celtic had one shot and two legitimate touches in the Besiktas penalty box. The Turkish side did little of note either, their former Rangers winger Vaclav Cerny routinely jeered.

Mercifully, the second half was far better.

Besiktas took the lead on 54 in calamitous circumstances. Celtic goalkeeper Sam Johnstone walloped a clearance off Leandro Trossard and the ball squirted to Ernest Poku. He absolutely skinned Lotomba, who chopped down the winger with his flailing attempt to salvage the situation. It was a clear spot-kick and while Johnstone partially redeemed himself by saving Olaitan's powerful penalty, the ball spun into the sky and towards the goal, where Olaitan followed up to tap home.

Lotomba tried to recover with a surging run from his own penalty box on 59 minutes that got the home crowd briefly energised. It was his last act, replaced by Colby Donovan on the hour mark. Duran and Osmand were also brought on for Forrest and Sebastien Tounekti.

Osmand did more in the first minute of action than the powderpuff Tounekti did in 60. The Englishman immediately made an impact, with Callum McGregor seizing on a loose ball and feeding the forward to find the bottom corner of Alexander Nubel's goal with an accurate strike. Celtic had something to build upon.

Besiktas had played comfortably up until this point but now looked a little rattled. Celtic embarked on their best period of the match. Nubel reacted smartly on 67 minutes to save a netbound Liam Scales header. Benjamin Nygren whistled an effort just over the bar eight minutes later. Suddenly the game was there for Celtic.

The ineffective striker Kasper Hogh was subbed off for Haissem Hassan as O'Neill turned to the Egyptian to unlock the Besiktas defence. But it was two earlier subs who made the difference again on 77 minutes, with Osmand slipping Duran in for the Colombian to round Nubel and send Celtic Park wild.

Celtic now had to hold on but their resistance was pierced by a vicious strike from Besiktas sub Orkun Kokcu from 25 yards on 86 minutes that fizzed beyond Johnstone and into the net. Never mind, though, when Duran is in town. The Colombian took in a sclaffed cross from Kieran Tierney a minute later and netted.

And this time, it was job done. Celtic Park roared its approval at full time.

#1931. Hull predicted lineup vs. Arsenal: Suspension blow for Sergej Jakirovic

By Ben Knapton | 05 Nov 2026 10:11

Hull City will have to manage without the banned Matt Crooks in Saturday's Premier League showdown with champions Arsenal at the Emirates.

The midfielder collected his fifth booking of the campaign in last weekend's 2-2 draw with Ipswich Town, meaning that he must serve a one-match suspension in gameweek 10.

However, Crooks was only a second-half substitute in the stalemate with Gary O'Neil's side, so his punishment should not have a major impact on Sergej Jakorivic's starting XI plans.

Instead, Regan Slater and Tim Iroegbunam - scorer of Hull's first last weekend - should continue their partnership, flanked by Mohamed Belloumi and Elliot Stroud in the Tigers' 5-4-1 system.

Oli McBurnie would have also been suspended for this game had he been cautioned last weekend, but the four-booking striker avoided the yellow card that would have rendered him unavailable.

#1926. Biggest Champions League away wins of all time after Lens 1-9 Como

By Darren Plant | 05 Nov 2026 10:29

Como are the talk of Europe after they recorded the biggest away win in Champions League history with a 9-1 victory at Lens.

Cesc Fabregas's reputation had already been enhanced with 4-1 triumphs over RB Leipzig and Manchester United earlier in the 2026-27 league phase, but Como's players have now etched their name in the record books - perhaps permanently - in numerous categories.

While Fabregas's focus has quickly turned back to domestic matters with Como sitting in fourth position in the Serie A table, football fans across the world are reminiscing over the kind of matches that have been pushed down the record books.

Here, Sports Mole provides a rundown of the biggest away victories in the Champions League era, including matches from the group stage or league phase onwards.

Prior to Como's exploits in France, there had been three instances of teams prevailing by 7-0 scorelines on away territory.

Liverpool are the team to have most recently prevailed by that score in October 2017, with Jurgen Klopp overseeing a routine win over NK Maribor in Slovenia with Roberto Firmino and Mohamed Salah both netting doubles.

Three days earlier, Luiz Adriano memorably scored five times for Shakhtar Donetsk in a 7-0 triumph at BATE Borisov of Belarus.

Meanwhile, Marseille were the first-ever 7-0 away victors in Champions League history, having cruised to success over Slovakian side MSK Zilina in 2010.

There are many other occasions where a team has prevailed by a six-goal margin, but Bayern Munich's 8-2 drubbing of Barcelona is the only example of that score for a designated away team.

However, "designated" is the key word here, with the quarter-final tie having taken place on neutral ground in Lisbon in August 2020 due to the coronavirus pandemic.

Some notable names have found themselves on the receiving end of a 7-1 scoreline, including Roma who were thrashed by Pep Guardiola's Bayern Munich at Stadio Olimpico in October 2014.

At six minutes and 12 seconds, Salah scored the fastest Champions League hat-trick in history when Liverpool beat Rangers at Ibrox eight years later.

As recently as March 2025, Arsenal cruised past Dutch giants PSV Eindhoven, while Lyon's trouncing of Dinamo Zagreb - which included four goals for Bafetimbi Gomis - was the first-ever 7-1 away scoreline in Champions League history in December 2011.

Hurzeler said his team deserved to win but also said they were lazy at times.

“That's what we expected,” said Hurzeler to TNT Sports after the match. “These games in the Conference League are different. You have to beat the low block, you have to understand what the opponents are looking for in the game and therefore you have to always be patient in these games and I think we did it today.

They had a good view of Hinshelwood taking the first shot of the match, a 25-yard drive tipped wide by Getafe keeper David Soria.

Rutter then rolled defender Sebastian Boselli but skewed his shot across goal and wide.

They threatened again when Hadjam got in behind, only to lose his footing when he tried to cut back inside, with Rutter unable to convert the loose ball.

Brighton were almost caught out from a Getafe corner on the half-hour mark with Bart Verbruggen forced into a sharp reaction save from Ivan Azon’s snap-shot.

The Seagulls should have scored when Rutter’s through-ball sent Hadjam racing clean through. Hadjam got to the ball before Soria but his finish clipped the keeper and came back off a post, with Yalcouye’s attempt from the rebound blocked on the line.

Azon threatened the Brighton goal again in first-half stoppage time but was once again denied by Verbruggen.

After the break some good build-up play from Rutter and Hadjam set up substitute Luka Vuskovic, but his shot was always curling away from the target.

The breakthrough arrived in the 64th minute when Pascal Gross lifted a diagonal ball towards the far post.

Overlapping full-back Costinha had acres of space on the right of the penalty area and cushioned his header back across goal.

Yalcouye’s timing was impeccable as he met the ball with a thumping header which flew past Soria and in off the crossbar.

Ibrahim Osman could have doubled the lead seconds after coming on but he could not make contact with Diego Gomez’s low cross.

#1921. Plymouth Argyle vs Alvechurch - prediction, team news, lineups

By Calum Burrowes | 05 Nov 2026 11:32, Last updated: 05 Nov 2026 11:42

Reaching the first round of the FA Cup for the second time in three seasons, seventh-tier Alvechurch travel to League One Plymouth Argyle hoping to continue their journey in football's oldest cup competition.

The Pilgrims head into Saturday's clash after a goalless draw with Reading last weekend that kept them in the top five, while the Church have already played five matches to reach this stage, most recently beating Spalding United 4-0 in a replay.

Plymouth Argyle will be hoping to avoid a cup upset on Saturday afternoon when they welcome their Midlands opponents to Home Park.

Tom Cleverley's side, who were knocked out in the first round of the FA Cup last season, head into the weekend in good form, having lost just two of their last seven outings in all competitions.

Since suffering back-to-back league defeats against Huddersfield Town and Stevenage, the Pilgrims have responded with a narrow victory over Cambridge United before sharing the points with Reading in a goalless draw.

After 14 League One matches, Plymouth have collected 23 points and sit comfortably in the playoff places, six points behind the league leaders as they look to mount a serious push for promotion back to the Championship.

The Devon outfit failed to progress beyond the opening round last season but enjoyed runs to the fourth and fifth rounds in the 2023-24 and 2024-25 campaigns, where they were eventually eliminated by Leeds United and Manchester City respectively.

Looking to reach the second round of the FA Cup for the second time in three years, Alvechurch make the journey south hoping some cup magic can help them produce one of the shocks of the season.

The Worcestershire-based side, who compete in the Southern League Premier Division Central, know they face a significant challenge against opponents four tiers above them, but arrive at Home Park in good form.

Led by former Wrexham and Cheltenham Town midfielder Kyle Storer, the Church are currently enjoying an unbeaten run of six matches in all competitions, including an impressive 3-1 away win against Leiston on Halloween and a 4-0 victory over Spalding in their FA Cup replay.

During that run, Storer's side have kept just one clean sheet but found the net 16 times, and will be hoping to showcase their attacking threat against League One opposition this weekend.

So far in this season's FA Cup, Alvechurch have overcome Wolverhampton City, Warwick, Cambridge and Spalding, with the latter requiring a replay after a 2-2 draw in the initial meeting.

As mentioned, the Church have previous experience of causing a cup upset, having beaten League One Cheltenham Town 2-1 away from home in the first round in November 2022, before reaching the second round and falling to Forest Green Rovers.

Ahead of a clash against opponents from several divisions below, Cleverley is likely to name a much-changed lineup and could stick with a similar XI to the one used in the EFL Trophy this season.

Murphy Cooper has been Plymouth's first-choice goalkeeper this season but withdrew from their match against Reading the day before the game due to a family issue.

James Storer came in for his league debut and impressed, meaning he could retain his place between the sticks for this one.

Teenager Sep Campbell, the club's youngest-ever goalscorer, has not featured for Plymouth since an EFL Trophy victory over Newport County but could return to the attack on Saturday.

As for the visitors, they reported no fresh injury concerns following their most recent outing and could name a similar starting XI to the one that secured their place in the next round a few weeks ago.

Miracle Okafor, who scored a brace in their 4-0 victory over Spalding, is likely to lead the line for Storer's men alongside Danny Newton.

Storer; Ross, Mitchell, Rendle; Edwards, Bakinson, White, MacKenzie; Amaechi, Campbell, Evans

Evans; Rask; Forsyth, Crowther, Ngandu, Sullivan; Reilly, Osborne, Stephens; Okafor, Newton

There is an obvious gulf in quality between these sides, and while Alvechurch have already shown they can trouble Football League opposition in the FA Cup, Plymouth should have enough to avoid an upset.

We expect the Pilgrims to progress comfortably into the next round with a 4-1 victory over the Church.

#1919. Jesus Owono’s team-mate defends goalkeeper after death of Jesus de Miguel

Andorra star Lautaro Spatz has offered his ‘sincere condolences’ to Jesus de Miguel’s loved ones following the footballer’s tragic death, while also sharing a message of support for his team-mate Jesus Owono.

Tenerife centre-forward De Miguel sustained severe head and chest injuries following a heavy collision with Andorra goalkeeper Owono, who was subsequently shown a red card for the challenge.

Owono had raced out of his his goal in an attempt to clear the ball when the deadly coming together occurred in the closing stages of Monday’s Spanish second-division contest.

It quickly became apparent that De Miguel required urgent medical attention and while the striker’s condition was described as ‘stable but serious’ after he was carried from the field and taken to hospital, his condition quickly deteriorated.

Sign up to our daily football newsletter, pick your team and get the latest news sent directly to your inbox every morning.

A heartbreaking statement on Tenerife’s social media pages on Tuesday morning confirmed that De Miguel has succumbed to his injuries, devastating news that has rocked the footballing world to its core.

Players and organisations have united in support of De Miguel’s friends and family in the hours that have followed, with heartfelt tributes shared and moments of silence observed across the globe.

Meanwhile, the Spanish FA postponed all Copa del Rey and Copa de la Reina matches that were scheduled to take place on Tuesday to allow for time to ‘grieve over this sad loss’.

It has also been announced that Tenerife’s Segunda Division clash with Granada – which had been due to kick off on Saturday – will be moved to a later date.

‘Following the tragic news of the death of Jesus de Miguel, a player for CD Tenerife, the LaLiga Hypermotion match between Granada CF and Tenerife, scheduled for Saturday, November 7th at the Nuevo Los Carmenes stadium, has been postponed,’ read a statement on Granada’s official website.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘The new date for the match is pending confirmation. The club reiterates its deepest condolences to the loved ones of Jesus de Miguel, as well as to the entire CD Tenerife family, sending them all strength and encouragement in these difficult times.’

Con el corazón encogido. Impresiona esto. Cientos de aficionados están despidiendo en estos momentos a Jesús de Miguel junto a la puerta 9 del Heliodoro. #jesusdemiguel pic.twitter.com/9aoHdlAh87

Reuters reported on Tuesday that police in Spain had launched an investigation for possible involuntary manslaughter in the wake of De Miguel’s death.

Under Spanish law, any death deemed to be non-natural automatically triggers a judicial inquiry.

However, criminal proceedings against Andorra shot-stopper Owono are ‘very unlikely’, according to Santa Cruz de Tenerife chief prosecutor Jose Luis Sanchez-Jauregui.

🖤 A moment of silence in memory of @CDTOficial forward Jesús de Miguel Alameda and the victims of last week’s train accident in Spain. pic.twitter.com/o1e4bQRX3E

Owono is yet to make a public statement in relation to the incident and Venancio Tomas Ndong Micha, the president of the Equatorial Guinean Football Federation, has said the 25-year-old was ‘experiencing profound distress and anguish’ following the news of De Miguel’s death.

Spanish radio station COPE reported that a section of supporters inside the Heliodoro Rodriguez Lopez stadium had yelled ‘murderer’ at Owono, appearing to blame the goalkeeper for the tragic circumstances that played out.

But Andorra defender Spatz, who helped carry De Miguel off the pitch on a stretcher, took to Instagram to defend Owono on Tuesday night, insisting his team-mate would ‘never intentionally hurt anyone’.

‘There are moments when football stops making sense. Moments that stay with you forever and make you realise just how fragile life can be. What we have experienced is something none of us will ever forget. A tragedy that has left us completely heartbroken, speechless and with a sadness that is difficult to put into words,’ Spatz wrote.

‘First of all, I would like to express my most sincere condolences and send all my love to the family, friends and loved ones of Jesus, as well as to the entire Chicharrera fanbase and the football community.

‘Since yesterday, the entire FC Andorra squad has been shocked, devastated and deeply affected by what has happened. It is a tragedy that we could never have imagined experiencing on a football pitch.

‘I would also like to say a few words about my team-mate, goalkeeper and friend, who has been deeply affected by what happened. Those of us who know him know what kind of person he is, how much he is suffering at this moment, and that he would never intentionally hurt anyone.

‘In football, accidents happen, but nobody could ever imagine that one of them could lead to such tragic consequences.’

The Andorra centre-back added: ‘Today, football doesn’t matter. All that matters is standing together in grief, showing the utmost respect and sending all our strength to the family and everyone suffering from this terrible loss.

‘Rest in peace, Demi. [broken heart emoji].’

A separate message on Andorra’s official website read: ‘We are deeply moved by the death of Jesus de Miguel. The first thing we want to do is extend our most sincere condolences to his family, CD Tenerife, and all those close to him.

‘We know that no words can ease such pain, but we want them to know that we stand by their side and deeply share their sadness.

‘We also want to extend all our support to CD Tenerife, its players, its technical staff, its workers, and its fans. We are deeply affected by what has happened and share the pain the club is experiencing. From the very first moment, we have been in contact with them and are at their disposal for anything they may need.

‘Likewise, we are in contact with LaLiga, the Government of Andorra, and the relevant organizations to offer all our collaboration and the necessary support during these very difficult times. We have also requested the postponement of the next match against RCD Mallorca, as we believe these are moments of profound grief in which respect and support for all those affected must prevail.

‘What has happened has had a great emotional impact on our players, the technical staff, and everyone who is part of FC Andorra. These are especially tough times for everyone, and we want to ensure that no one has to face them alone. For this reason, the club is providing psychological support to all those who need it.

‘We are a team, on and off the field. Now more than ever, we must stand together, support each other, and take care of one another.

‘All of football and all of sports are in mourning. These are moments of profound sadness in which we must remain united, support those who need it most, and show the utmost respect.

‘Our most sincere condolences to Jesús’s family and to everyone at CD Tenerife. Rest in peace, Jesus.’
