The London club’s manager, Pierre Sage, who worked with Fofana at Lyon, is thought to have personally intervened in an attempt to persuade the player to move to South London. By late afternoon, Palace appeared to have got their man having also offered more money to Lyon and higher wages to the player and fees to his agency.

Sunderland, though, refused to concede defeat and, according to reports in France, launched a counter proposal of their own led by French owners Kyril Louis-Dreyfus who flew to Lyon to try and clinch the deal.

At one stage, it was even claimed that the player had two different private jets waiting at the airport to take him to either London or the North East depending on who he elected to sign for.

That was later refuted, although it is understood the player did have a medical in Lyon that could be viewed by both clubs before he made up his mind. That gave his representatives more time to thrash the terms of a deal with both clubs.

However, having failed to board an earlier flight to Lyon after talks with Palace advanced, Sunderland’s late push belatedly persuaded the 21-year-old to head to Wearside, and he is due to be unveiled on Wednesday morning.

Arsenal had also been linked with the player earlier this week but were not willing to match the asking price for Fofana who they viewed as a project player.

Mykhailo Mudryk’s loan move from Chelsea to Spurs has been confirmed.

Forgive the personal opinion but this is my favourite deal of the window. Mudryk played some of his best football under Roberto De Zerbi at Shakhtar Donetsk. The Spurs head coach has even described Mudryk as “my son”, and has previously tipped him as a future Ballon d’Or winner.

After so long out of the game, Mudryk now has a coach who knows exactly how to get the best out of him. It might not work at all. Mudryk may need months to rediscover his match sharpness after so long out. But I am very excited to find out.

Misha is Spurs 🇺🇦 pic.twitter.com/aW4VKFbvam

I think Chelsea come out of this deadline day very well. Sold a player who didn't want to play for them for a British record-equalling fee and signed a top target in double-quick time for a decent price in this market and in the circumstances. Strong window overall #cfc

Manuel Ángel, 22, has moved to Craven Cottage. Fulham describe their new signings as “a two-footed central midfield player, comfortable with the ball at his feet, is intelligent with his movement, and has a keen eye for a pass.” All that for an undisclosed fee.

But a loan would only have been possible with an obligation to buy yet United were not interested in committing themselves to a permanent deal for the player.

Nottingham Forest have established an unwanted reputation for hectic business on deadline day but today is very likely to be a sign that things are changing.

Forest are not expected to make any signings before the deadline and are perfectly happy with their squad.

The big signings have been Liam Delap (£45m from Chelsea), Ousmane Diomande (£34m from Sporting CP) and Daniel Munoz (£20m from Crystal Palace).

Forest did want to sign a central midfielder, with bids for Tottenham’s Lucas Bergvall and Everton’s Harrison Armstrong rejected, but the general feeling is one of calm.

Arnaud Kalimuendo is also going to stay at the City Ground despite strong interest from Eintracht Frankfurt in re-signing him after he impressed on loan over the second half of last season.

Chelsea have agreed a £47m fee with Monaco to sign midfielder Lamine Camara. It’s late in the day, but all sides are optimistic this one will get done.

Manchester United made a deadline day enquiry to rivals Manchester City about Rayan Ait-Nouri but were told the Algeria left-back was not available.

Meanwhile, Everton have made a late move for forward Joshua Zirkzee.

Chelsea’s transfer window might not be over. Sources in France believe the club may still sign Lamine Camara from Monaco before the window shuts. Chelsea had a £38m bid for Camara turned down earlier today but the door has reopened after Folarin Balogun’s proposed move to Everton stalled. Stand by your beds...

Iliman Ndiaye has been confirmed as a Manchester City signing. He moves on a five-year deal from Everton with the deal worth £65m.

The fee means Premier League spending has now surpassed the previous record for a summer window which stood at £3.14bn. The running tally now stands at £3.193bn.

Ndiaye says: “I’ve worked my whole life for an opportunity like this. City are one of the best clubs in the world and I’ve seen them win everything as I’ve grown up.

“To be able to write my own chapter in a story that special is the chance of a lifetime and I’m determined to grab it with both hands.

“It’s not always been easy in my career, but I always had the belief that I could play for a team challenging for the biggest prizes and now I’m here. It feels so good.

“I love to play with the ball on the floor in an attacking team that wants to score as many goals as possible. That’s why I know this is the perfect fit.

“City fans can rest assured that I will give my all to bring more success to this incredible club.”

Welcome to City, Iliman 🩵 pic.twitter.com/u3WWUpVQOg

Harry Amass looks like he’s staying at Old Trafford and Louis Page’s proposed move to United from Leicester is off after a failure to reach an agreement. Willem II are trying to sign Chido Obi on loan. As reported earlier, not expecting United to sign a left-back, barring a dramatic turn of events, so not the deadline day or end to the window United fans will have hoped for.

Significant – and dispiriting – news for Everton. Folarin Balogun has failed a medical and it appears that his £40m move from Monaco is off. The club are yet to confirm any news but the indications are this is a devastating blow for both the player and the club.

Wilfried Gnonto has joined Fiorentina on a season-long loan with a £15m buy option. That could open the door for Jean-Matteo Bahoya to sign from Eintracht Frankfurt.

Usurped as Chelsea’s first-choice goalkeeper, Sanchez is on his way to Italy where he will play under Cesc Fabregas. Como also completed the signing of former Juventus and Everton striker Moise Kean today.

Fabregas said: “Robert brings experience at the highest level and qualities that suit the way we want to play. He is a strong goalkeeper with a big presence, but he is also very comfortable with the ball and can help us build from the back.”

He joins from Spurs on a season-long loan and the deal features a buy option. Sunderland’s statement reads: “A commanding centre-back, Danso has won hearts throughout his career, with his committed performances.” Who knew the Austria centre-half was the object of so much affection?

Nottingham Forest defender Morato has completed his move to West Ham United.

Morato has joined the Championship club on an initial loan with West Ham holding an option to make the move permanent.

West Ham’s manager Nuno Espirito Santo signed the Brazilian centre-back during his spell with Forest.

Crystal Palace are having a frantic end to the transfer window, with Ben Chilwell also a deal they are pursuing.

The former England left-back, 29, is at Strasbourg where he is in the final year of his contract. Palace are also trying for Quinten Timber from Marseille and are still in the race for Lyon’s Malick Fofana.

Ethan Nwaneri has completed his loan move from Arsenal to Borussia Dortmund. A lot of Arsenal fans will be pleased he hasn’t been sold, which was a real possibility this summer. Hopefully this move is more successful than his time in Marseille in the second half of last season, when the chaos at the club did not help the teenager to settle.

Liverpool’s last significant business for the window is done with the completion of the £30m deal for goalkeeper Lucca Brughmans from Genk. The 18-year-old will remain in Belgium, to play the season with his current club.

He has been bought with the future in mind and Liverpool are covering all bases, as Alisson Becker – who has been the undisputed No 1 since he arrived in 2018 – is now in the final year of his contract. Liverpool also spent £33m on Giorgi Mamardashvili last summer.

Alisson could have left this summer, with Juventus initially keen to sign him. Either way, this points to Liverpool making plans for a new generation.

Never quite lived up to his billing as a Berbatov-Havertz hybrid, scoring 11 goals in 53 appearances for Newcastle in all competitions last season when the idea of him leading the line was slowly abandoned. Serie A should suit him better, and Newcastle have confirmed his move to Italy.

Crystal Palace midfielder Justin Devenny is undergoing a medical at Championship club Stoke City.

Devenny, 22, is a Northern Ireland international and is close to joining Stoke on a permanent basis.

Palace midfielder David Ozoh could also leave before the deadline, with Derby County keen to re-sign their former loan signing again.

Speaking about the Enzo Fernández deal on Sky Sports, Carragher said: “It pushes them above Chelsea. Myself and plenty of others felt Chelsea would have a really good season, and I still believe that.

“A lot of that is on the back of no European football, having a new manager and the front three they have got.

“But losing Enzo Fernandez, who for me over the last two or three years has been one of the big players for Chelsea... they’ve always had five or six top players but maybe not a lot around them.

“They’ve let one of them go, to Man City, it’s a huge fee but City look a lot stronger now and I’d say they are going to be the main challengers to Arsenal.”

Crystal Palace are making a late move for Quinten Timber in a deal from Marseille. The 25-year-old Netherlands international has been on Palace’s radar for a central midfield role. He is the twin brother of Arsenal defender Jurrien.

According to Sky Germany, Brighton are keen on 21-year-old Chema Andrés from Stuttgart. He started 14 games in the Bundesliga last season, and came through the ranks at Real Madrid.

Leeds are lining up Eintracht Frankfurt forward Jean-Matteo Bahoya as Willy Gnonto is waiting on move to Fiorentina.

Chelsea had been holding off from sanctioning Enzo Fernández’s move to Manchester City while they searched for a new midfielder of their own.

But City’s willingness to agree a £125m package has convinced Chelsea to give the green light to the Fernández move without any guarantees over an incoming signing.

Chelsea still have a few hours to try to make something happen, having had a bid for Lamine Camara turned down.

But Chelsea ultimately felt they had no choice but to let Fernández, who made it clear he wanted to leave, go in the best interests of the club.

Chelsea believe they have a strong squad, regardless of whether or not a new player is signed today, and will continue to weigh up their options.

The medicals are under way for Jack Grealish, Ainsley Maitland-Niles and Folarin Balogun at Everton but there is no clarity on when all three deals will be concluded. It must be stressed that no issues are envisaged and they will be the only additions to the squad before the window closes. No further departures are expected, either.

On the other side of the city, things are winding down for Liverpool. Harvey Elliott’s loan to Valencia will be officially announced in due course. It is a straight loan, without an obligation to buy.

Fulham are progressing quite quickly on three deals: Hugo Larsson (Frankfurt), Manuel Angel (Real Madrid) and David Affengruber (Elche).

Sunderland now believe their move for Malick Fofana is back on despite Crystal Palace’s attempt to hijack the deal...

Chelsea have agreed a £125m package to sell Enzo Fernández to Manchester City so the saga is finally coming to a close.

Chelsea will be happy with a fee that equals the British transfer record and City head coach Enzo Maresca will be delighted to land his top target.

It feels like a win-win all round as Fernández wanted to leave Chelsea and the club wanted over £120m after their initial deadline to do a deal expired.

It remains to be seen if Chelsea land any of their three main deadline day targets with a few hours of the window to go.

Chelsea had a bid rejected for Lamine Camara, Roma have not been playing ball on Manu Kone and the identity of the mystery Premier League target has not yet emerged.

Newcastle insist the only deals they are working on for the rest of the day are the departures of Nick Woltemade on loan to Juventus and Sean Neave to Wolverhampton Wanderers.

Multiple sources deny there is any chance of Jacob Murphy leaving for Nottingham Forest despite claims of a second bid being rejected today.

High drama on Wearside where Sunderland fear their deal to sign Malick Fofana from Lyon has been hijacked by Crystal Palace.

Nobody has told Sunderland the deal is off yet, but the fact they are also lining up an alternative in the shape of Dodi Lukébakio shows they are worried.

It is understood Sunderland have made contact with Benfica this afternoon to discuss terms for Lukébakio, who is another Belgium international.

Crystal Palace are believed to have offered more money to Lyon and higher wages to Fofana which could be enough to swing things in their favour.

Manchester United are in discussions about signing the 18-year-old Leicester midfielder Louis Page. Talks ongoing with Leicester but there are no guarantees a deal will happen at this stage.

As things stand, Joshua Zirkzee seems more likely to stay at United than go. The prospects of bringing in a left-back are also fading.

West Ham are in a state of flux, trying to find their way in the Championship, and they have failed with a bid to take Michael Keane from Everton on loan. They had offers from Werder Bremen and Sevilla, too, to take Edson Álvarez out on a season-long loan. The interest from Sevilla in the Mexican was strong and the proposal would have covered all of Álvarez’s wages but West Ham were looking to recoup a significant loan fee to sanction it. That detail led to the deal falling through.

When Newcastle United’s recruitment team finalised their list of priority targets back in the spring Matías Fernández-Pardo featured prominently.

There was excitement about what he could bring to the team. There was a buzz of possibility. The 21-year-old forward had impressed everyone, from scouts to decision makers. The call to make him one of their first-choice targets, alongside Switzerland international Johan Manzambi, was unanimous. Just as it had been when Newcastle identified Alexander Isak as their leading target back in the summer of 2022.

These meetings are a place for ideas to be shared and different targets pushed. Everyone had their own opinion and various favourites, but Fernández-Pardo was, in the words of one member of Newcastle’s recruitment taskforce “the one”.

In the Scottish Premiership, deals can be completed until 5pm on Thursday, September 3.

Former Wolves, Fulham and West Ham winger Adama Traore has joined La Liga side Deportivo A Coruna.

Sunderland had seemingly beaten Arsenal to the Lyon winger’s signature but reports have emerged that Crystal Palace are attempting to hijack Fofana’s Wearside move...

We’re still awaiting official confirmation of Mykhailo Mudryk’s loan move to Tottenham Hotspur. It would mean a reunion with Roberto De Zerbi, under whom the Ukrainian played at Shakhtar Donetsk.

When asked about Mudryk in 2022, the then Brighton head coach said: “Mykhailo has the potential for a top career. In my opinion, he can also win the Ballon d’Or. He is a player of the highest level but he is also very sensitive.”

De Zerbi added: “He needs affection. We will see if he matches his potential.”

Gabriel Jesus has completed his move from Arsenal to Barcelona in a deal worth about £9m. It’s a fantastic move for the Brazilian, who had declined in importance at Arsenal after a succession of serious injuries. Arsenal would have hoped for a higher fee for a player of his reputation but his enormous salary, believed to have been worth about £250,000 a week, was always going to be problematic as they looked for buyers.

Danns is the one who can keep the record going.

Sam Johnstone is heading to Celtic ahead of a loan deal from Wolves.

The 33-year-old, capped four times by England under Gareth Southgate, is travelling to Scotland this afternoon to completed the formalities of the deal including a medical.

Ainsley Maitland-Niles has emerged as a prime target for Everton, as they look to find a solution to their right-back conundrum. The former Arsenal defender, who is now at Lyon, has been the subject of a £5m offer and the indication is that he has now taken over from Kenny Tete as the preferred option. Everton, historically, have always pushed things to the wire on transfer deadline day and this one is proving to be no different.

Benfica are in talks about loaning Argentina Under-23 forward Claudio Echeverri from Manchester City, It’s likely to be a season long loan with an option to buy if finalised.

Fabio Vieira has completed his move from Arsenal to Hamburg, in a deal believed to be worth about £9m. Southampton forward Cameron Archer is on course to sign for Auxerre on a season-long loan.

Archer has been a target for a number of Championship clubs this summer but a deal has been problematic because of his £35,000-a-week wages.

It is understood Southampton have been demanding that his salary be paid in full, which has scared off interested clubs in the second tier.

Chelsea will hold off sanctioning Enzo Fernández’s move to Manchester City until they are confident of making at least one signing of their own.

Telegraph Sport understands that Chelsea have already rejected one proposal from City for Fernández during club-to-club talks and are demanding a fee and payment terms that are favourable to them.

Chelsea also have three separate targets of their own as potential deadline signings – Lamine Camara, Manu Kone and one mystery target from the Premier League.

Monaco have already rejected a £38.5m bid from Chelsea for Camara. Roma manager Gian Piero Gasperini wants to keep Kone, although negotiations continue. And there is a third target from the Premier League, who is not believed to be Morgan Gibbs-White.

Chelsea must make significant progress on one of their targets before they will sanction Fernández’s sale – and City must make another bid that is more favourable to the club.

Monaco have rejected an opening €45m bid from Chelsea for midfielder Lamine Camara. It now remains to be seen if the club increase that offer.

Sunderland have been trying to sign a winger all summer and it appears that they have finally got their man in Lyon’s Malick Fofana.

Arsenal had been linked with a move for the 21-year old Belgium international.

Of Koné, former France manager Didier Deschamps said: “He’s very effective at winning the ball back, but he shouldn’t be limited to that role of defensive midfielder, because he also makes a difference in his use of the ball.”

Austria centre-back David Affengruber has emerged as potential deadline-day deal for Fulham as they look to bolster Alvaro Arbeloa’s defence.

The Elche player has been in La Liga for two years playing regularly and fits the data model at Craven Cottage.

Fulham are also trying deals for Real Madrid’s Manuel Angel and Eintracht Frankfurt’s Hugo Larsson as midfield options.

Sunderland are expected to complete the signing of centre-back Kevin Danso from Tottenham Hotspur with the player travelling to Wearside last night for the first part of his medical.

The Austria international will initially join on loan with an obligation to make the move permanent for £25m next year.

Danso had made it clear he wanted to leave Tottenham this summer in search of regular first-team football.

Eintracht Frankfurt are in talks with Nottingham Forest over another loan move for forward Arnaud Kalimuendo.

Frankfurt signed the Frenchman on loan in January and are negotiating a return for Forest’s £26m signing from Rennes.

Oliver Glasner, Forest’s head coach, had been intent on keeping Kalimuendo but it is understood Frankfurt’s strong interest has altered the club’s thinking.

Morato, the centre-back, is expected to join West Ham United on loan.

Forest are exploring potential signings but are determined to stay calm and only pursue deals that make financial sense. A winger and a No 6 are the two priority targets if there are deals to be done.

On Tuesday evening, the Tottenham and Brazil forward posted an emotional message on Instagram amid reports of a possible move back to Everton.

He wrote: “After everything I’ve been through in recent years, I decided that never again would others decide my future for me.

“I went through a lot of bad things during this time, and almost all of them happened because of decisions made by other people. Pressure, threats, retaliation – none of that scares me. I’ve been through worse, believe me!

“I have always made it clear at every opportunity that my departure to another place would also have to be good for the club. If it wasn’t, I would never accept it... just as I didn’t accept it when everything here was falling apart and they needed me.”

Richarlison added: “I stayed and gave my all. So, I hope they treat my situation with the same respect that I have always had for Spurs and for all the people who worked with me during this period. Just don’t try to decide for me.”

“If Spurs and Everton reach an agreement, I will return to the club of my heart. My intention was indeed to go back to the place where I was very happy.

“But negotiations were being done the way other people wanted, and it won’t be that way anymore. Despite all this turmoil, I have a contract with Spurs and I will remain at the club’s disposal.”

It will be good news for Arsenal if Folarin Balogun completes his £40m move to Everton today. When Arsenal sold Balogun to Monaco in 2023, they negotiated a sell-on clause of 17.5 per cent. According to my maths, that means Arsenal will get £7m from this transfer. Not to be sniffed at!

Hull City are close to agreeing a fee of around £7.5m for Stoke City winger Sorba Thomas.

The Wales international has been a long-term target for Hull and negotiations are now approaching a conclusion.

Thomas has been pushing a move through and is expected to leave Stoke after one full season.

As has become the norm this summer Acun Ilicali has posted a cryptic message on X, which has prompted speculation among Hull City fans. The club has been linked with Everton holding midfielder Tim Iroegbunam.

Newcastle will complete the £51m signing of forward Matias Fernandez-Pardo from Lille today but that is expected to be it in terms of incomings.

The Belgium international will become the club’s eighth signing of the summer and his versatility – he can play as a centre forward, a No 10 or out wide – means there are no more gaps to fill in the squad.

In an ideal world, Newcastle would have liked to sign another defender but none of their targets were still on the market. With Dan Burn due to return from injury in a few weeks, they have four centre-backs while new arrival Amar Dedic can play on both sides as a full-back.

In terms of outgoings, Joe Willock and Jacob Murphy are expected to stay at the club despite interest from Nottingham Forest and Besiktas. Young striker Sean Neave will be allowed to leave on loan. The 19-year-old has offers from clubs in the Championship and League One but Newcastle want him to go somewhere he has the best chance of getting regular first-team football.

City have been this summer’s selling kings and have had six players leave the club in deals worth more than £45m. Compare that to the summer when Pep Guardiola first arrived at the club, in 2016, when City generated just £23m from sales and made losses on Edin Dzeko and Stevan Jovetic, while Martín Demichelis departed on a free transfer.

Fast forward to this summer and more than £300m worth of players have been sold, with a further £60m arriving at the end of the season when Omar Marmoush’s loan to Tottenham Hotspur becomes permanent.

Given how Jaissle wants Newcastle to play, it is plain to see why Fernandez-Pardo appeals to him. Quick, direct and only 21 – he would surely fit right in at St James’ Park.

A post shared by Ligue 1 McDonald's (@ligue1mcdonalds)

The Leeds wide man has a medical booked with Fiorentina today. He made a handful of appearances for Daniel Farke’s side during pre-season but has not featured since the start of the 2026-27 campaign.

✈️ L'arrivo di Gnonto a Firenze ⚜️ pic.twitter.com/nEFngsyxQP

Very unlikely that Liverpool will be doing any major incoming business but there may yet be some departures. Jayden Danns, who broke through three years ago and played in the 2024 League Cup final defeat of Chelsea, is attracting interest from clubs in Europe, who want to take him on loan. Danns, a promising striker, has had injury issues and is working his way back to full fitness but his long-term ambition is to prove to Andoni Iraola that he can be part of his squad.

Fax machines are whirring as the clock continues to tick towards the transfer deadline, but who does your club need to sign? Let us know in the comments below!

Aston Villa are to confirm the signings of £50m winger Ibrahim Mbaye and £25m centre-back Taylor Harwood-Bellis this morning.

Mbaye and Harwood-Bellis takes the number of Villa’s signings this summer to 10, with Unai Emery ruling out any more additions after the 1-0 defeat by Arsenal last night.

Emery also disclosed that forward Tammy Abraham will be staying at Villa Park, amid interest from Ipswich Town.

The one player who could leave today is Jamaica international Leon Bailey, who has interest from clubs in Europe, and Hull City.

Nottingham Forest can confirm Omari Hutchinson has joined AC Milan on a season-long loan deal, with the Italian club holding an option to make the transfer permanent.Everyone at Nottingham Forest wishes Omari all the best for his time in Italy. pic.twitter.com/fSv1uNGh2Y

Fulham remain locked in discussions with Rayo Vallecano to agree a fee for right-back Andrei Ratiu, with the Romania international having confirmed he wants to join Alvaro Arbeloa’s side. The spin-off with this deal is that it will accelerate Kenny Tete’s switch to Everton, for a fee in the region of £9.5m.

On the subject of right-backs, Nathan Patterson, who has had a difficult time at Everton, has been granted permission to travel to Italy to undergo a medical with Torino.

Matias Fernandez-Pardo is on the verge of joining Newcastle United, and Luke Edwards reported that the forward’s arrival is likely to pave the way for Nick Woltemade’s departure.

The German enjoyed a fruitful start to life in England after signing last summer, scoring seven Premier League goals before the turn of the year, but could only manage one goal in the second half of the season. While Eddie Howe experimented with Woltemade in a more withdrawn No 10 role, there was a clear drop-off in his game-time after Christmas.

Newcastle are ready to pay around £51m to sign Fernandez-Pardo after holding face-to-face talks with Lille last week. The 21-year-old is a versatile attacker and Newcastle identified him as a top target months ago. If they can complete a deal, it could speed up the departure of Nick Woltemade, who is wanted by Juventus.

The Brazilian has asked to leave Spurs and has been linked to a move back to Everton. However, his hopes of returning to Merseyside may have taken a hit on Monday night, when Everton agreed a £40m deal with Monaco for striker Folarin Balogun.

Brighton are keen to sign Azeez from Millwall and have made multiple offers for the forward. Millwall want at least £15m for Azeez, who scored 11 goals in the Championship last season. Ipswich Town have previously shown interest in Azeez.

Leeds are signing Melvin Bard on loan from Nice. One-season deal for the 25-year-old who will compete for a place in the first-team under Daniel Farke.

We’re expecting four departures from Arsenal today. Nwaneri to Dortmund on loan (see my colleague Mike McGrath’s post below), Gabriel Martinelli to Al-Hilal, Gabriel Jesus to Barcelona and Fabio Vieira to Hamburg. Those deals should raise around £70m.

Will there be any incomings? The Julian Alvarez situation seems unlikely to develop in Arsenal’s favour, barring a dramatic change of heart. As reported by Telegraph Sport yesterday, Lyon winger Malick Fofana is a potential option.

Borussia Dortmund have been trying to close out a loan deal for Arsenal winger Ethan Nwaneri, as reported by Telegraph Sport yesterday. The German club have previously attempted to land the 19-year-old and this time want him on a deal for the season.

It is expected to be another busy deadline day in the Premier League, with many clubs still hoping to finalise deals before the transfer window shuts at 11pm. Here, Telegraph Sport identifies 10 potential high-profile moves that could yet go through.

This has been the most dramatic and relentless saga of the European transfer window. The situation, as far as we understand it, is as follows: Barcelona want Alvarez and Alvarez wants Barcelona, but Atletico Madrid refuse to sell him to Barcelona. Arsenal want Alvarez, and Atletico are more open to selling him to Arsenal, but Alvarez only wants Barcelona. For a move to happen, it will require one party to change their mind. Either Atletico decides to sell to Barcelona, or Alvarez decides he will join Arsenal.

Another long-running saga. Chelsea are well aware of City’s interest in Fernandez but want a massive fee for the Argentina international, having initially valued him at £120m. City have the cash and the space in the squad after saying goodbye to Rodri, Tijani Reijnders, Nico Gonzalez and Bernardo Silva this summer. Fernandez has not featured in Chelsea’s last two games.

As reported by Telegraph Sport last week, Chelsea have identified Monaco midfielder Camara as a target amid the uncertainty over Fernandez’s future. French reports on Monday suggested the move may have stalled, however. The clock is ticking.

Spurs had been working on a deal to sign Ndiaye from Everton but they now appear to have fallen behind City in the race for the winger, as a consequence of City failing in their attempt to sign Cody Gakpo from Liverpool. City are ready to complete the hijack on deadline day.

A deal that, as of Monday night, is regarded as unlikely to happen. As with their interest in Brighton’s Yankuba Minteh, Liverpool have so far been unable to strike a deal with Crystal Palace for Sarr, who scored 21 goals in 45 games last season. Liverpool would only allow Gakpo to leave if a replacement, such as Sarr, can be signed.

Burnley are one of a host of Championship clubs who are interested in the young Manchester United left-back Harry Amass. There have been talks over a potential permanent deal but a loan cannot be ruled out. The 19-year-old joined United from Watford in 2023.

Everton have reached an agreement with Manchester City to sign Jack Grealish on another season long loan. It has been a very busy summer of outgoings at City and Grealish will be the latest to depart as he prepares to return to Merseyside. He started well at Everton last season before injury in January derailed his campaign.

A big year ahead for the English midfielder.

Tottenham are set to complete a double deal for Chelsea pair Mykhailo Mudryk and Tosin Adarabioyo after missing out on Iliman Ndiaye.

Spurs will take Mudryk on loan for the season having seen their attempt to land Ndiaye fail when Manchester City agreed a £65m deal with Everton.

Mudryk, 25, worked with Spurs head coach Roberto De Zerbi at Shakthtar Donetsk, in the winger’s homeland Ukraine, before his £85m move to Chelsea in 2023.

Leeds United had shown interest but instead he will be reunited with De Zerbi, effectively taking Ndiaye’s place as a wide-forward option.

Adarabioyo will be a permanent deal to Spurs as they are not allowed to loan two players from a Premier League club.

Good morning and welcome to live coverage of transfer deadline day. We are deep into stoppage time in this summer window and we will bring you the key developments as teams scramble to get last-minute deals over the line before the full-time whistle blows at 11pm.

Enzo Fernández remains a City target, and his omission from Xabi Alonso’s match-day squad against Brighton and Hove Albion on Sunday has only added weight to the feeling that he might reunite with former Chelsea head coach Enzo Maresca. City would be required to meet the Londoners’ £120m asking price, which is just shy of Alexander Isak’s £125m British record fee.

Meanwhile, Julián Alvarez’s situation at Atlético Madrid continues to be monitored by Arsenal. The Argentina forward’s dream move to Barcelona appears a no-goer as Atlético remain steadfast in their refusal to sell to their La Liga rivals. While this could bring Arsenal into the picture, it is understood that Alvarez – who missed three training sessions last week and did not travel to Sevilla with Diego Simeone’s squad on Saturday – is not pursuing a return to England.

A Mohamed Salah-shaped hole on Liverpool’s right flank has been filled by Bradley Barcola after the club agreed a £123m deal with Paris St-Germain. His signing looked as though it might trigger Cody Gakpo’s move away from Anfield as the winger had been linked with a move to Manchester City, but it appears that the Netherlands international will stay put. Maresca’s side have instead hijacked Spurs’ move for Iliman Ndiaye, and the north London outfit pivoted to take Myhailo Mudryk and Tosin Adarabioyo from Chelsea, on loan and permanent deals respectively. Liverpool could yet swoop for Brighton’s Yankuba Minteh or Ismaïla Sarr.

Newcastle United appeared to have reached their nadir this summer after Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali, Bruno Guimarães and Eddie Howe departed, but Matthias Jaissle has breathed life into St James’ Park by delivering an exciting brand of football that leans on the team’s explosive pace in forward positions. Lille’s Matias Fernandez-Pardo would fit this system and is on the brink of joining Newcastle in a deal worth £51m, which could signal Nick Woltemade’s exit.

Barcola is the window’s most expensive acquisition, followed by Morgan Rogers who was prised away from Aston Villa to the tune of £118m, and has already hit the ground running for the Londoners. He cost £2m more than his England team-mate Elliot Anderson, who swapped Nottingham Forest for Manchester City. Elite midfielders have proved a gilded commodity with seven of the Premier League’s top 10 most expensive acquisitions coming in the middle of the park. The departures of Rodri, Casemiro and others will have played their part.

Praying for a deadline-day saviour or counting down the seconds until the window slams shut on directors of football hoping to lure away your club’s next big thing? Let us know in the comments and join the conversation as the day unfolds.

#1787. Arsenal 'track new forward signing' after Mikel Arteta transfer targets revealed

Your weekly briefing on Arsenal, featuring team news and expert analysis from Matt Verri

Arsenal have added Antonio Nusa to their list of transfer targets ahead of the January window, according to new reports.

While the Gunners spent big in the summer - adding Ezri Konsa, Bruno Guimaraes and Christos Tzolis to their squad - not bringing in at least one more attacker was considered a risky strategy.

In fact, upon allowing Gabriel Martinelli, Leandro Trossard and Gabriel Jesus to leave permanently, there is an argument that Arsenal ended the summer window weaker in attack than when they started it.

As such, it has been widely reported that the club plan to prioritise signing a forward when the transfer window reopens.

The Mirror, this week, have ‘revealed’ Bournemouth’s Eli Junior Kroupi and Juventus wonderkid Kenan Yildiz are both on Mikel Arteta’s radar, though a January move for either could prove difficult.

Now, the Sun claim the Gunners are also tracking RB Leipzig winger Nusa and have been scouting the Norway international this season.

Predominantly a left-sided attacker, Nusa can also operate on the right flank and has made an impressive start to the campaign by scoring six goals and weighing in with seven assists in 14 appearances across all competitions.

The 21-year-old was on target for Leipzig in their 3-2 defeat to Manchester City in the Champions League on Wednesday night, prompting excitement among some Arsenal fans on social media as a result.

However, the aforementioned report states a deal taking Nusa to north London at the start of 2027 will be difficult to pull off as Leipzig view the winger as a key player and do not want to sell him in the middle of the season.

Furthermore, the Bundesliga club's stance his strengthened after selling Yan Diomande to Real Madrid in the summer for around £120million, meaning they are under no financial pressure to cash in on Nusa.

#1786. Portsmouth vs Stoke City - prediction, team news, lineups

By Ben Sully | 05 Nov 2026 15:52, Last updated: 05 Nov 2026 20:34

Two in-form sides will face off when Portsmouth welcome Stoke City to Fratton Park for Saturday's Championship encounter.

Pompey head into the weekend in 10th position in the Championship table, while the Potters are in fourth spot and a point adrift of automatic promotion.

Portsmouth share the league's current longest unbeaten run with rivals Southampton after winning four and drawing two of their last six matches.

Pompey continued their impressive run of form with a dramatic 3-1 victory over promotion hopefuls Swansea in Tuesday's clash at Fratton Park.

After seeing his opener cancelled out by Zan Vipotnik's 85th-minute penalty, Terry Devlin put his team back in front in the second minute of stoppage time, shortly before Thomas Waddingham netted in a second straight home game to wrap up all three points.

As a result, Pompey, who have battled relegation in the last two seasons, are sitting just one point adrift from the top eight and four points away from automatic promotion, sparking dreams of ending their 16-year wait for Premier League football.

They will go into Saturday's fixture with hopes of recording four consecutive home league wins for the first time since January 2025.

The fourth win on that occasion came via a 2-1 scoreline against Stoke, which may be a good omen as they look to extend their five-game unbeaten home streak.

Stoke, meanwhile, have lost just one of their last 11 Championship outings, representing a significant improvement from starting the campaign with three consecutive league defeats.

In fact, they have won three of their last four outings since suffering their most recent loss in a home clash against Middlesbrough last month.

The Potters recorded clean sheets in wins against Derby County and Preston North End, either side of a goalless draw against Preston North End.

Mark Robins's side missed out on a fourth consecutive clean sheet in their midweek away clash against Blackburn Rovers, but crucially they left Ewood Park with all three points after claiming a 2-1 victory thanks to a Jack McGlynn effort and an own goal.

That result represented a fourth consecutive win on the road and made it five consecutive away games without defeat since losing to Wolverhampton Wanderers at the end of August.

The Potters enjoyed success on their last trip to Fratton Park in October 2025, when a 70th-minute own goal proved enough to fire them to a 1-0 victory.

Portsmouth remain without Benjamin Arthur, Connor Ogilvie, Mark Kosznovszky, John Swift, Luke Brooke-Smith, Keshi Anderson and Colby Bishop.

Striker Marko Milovanovic has been ruled out of Saturday’s contest after he pulled up with a quad issue in the second half against Swansea.

Midfielder Ilyas Mohamed was also forced off with a calf issue in Tuesday’s win, and while it is believed to be a minor problem, it is unclear whether he will be ready for the weekend.

As for the Potters, they head to Fratton Park without the injured trio of Eric Bocat, Lamine Cisse and Ato Ampah.

Aaron Cresswell and Sam Gallagher are on the verge of returning from injury, but it remains to be seen whether they will prove their fitness in time for Saturday’s away trip.

One certainty is that midfielder Ethan Galbraith will return to the fold after serving a one-match ban for an accumulation of yellow cards.

Schmid; Devlin, Poole, Dia, Meghoma; Pack, Adams; Segecic, Bailey, Kavuma-McQueen; Shade

Johansson; Wilmot, Lawal, Graham; Johnson, Soumare, Galbraith, Bombino; McGlynn, Devenny, Bozenik

Brimming with confidence, Portsmouth and Stoke will both fancy their chances of claiming the spoils this weekend, but with both teams proving tough to beat, we think they could cancel one another out in a score draw.

#1785. Sky Germany: Krösche heading for Milan but compensation must be discussed – the situation

Sources in Germany are confirming that Markus Krösche should be announced by AC Milan in the coming weeks, ready to start in January.

It is seemingly not a very well-kept secret by this point that Milan are looking to appoint Krösche as their new Head of Football, having made an attempt to get him in the summer. Sources in Italy have claimed things are done, but their German colleagues have always been a bit more hesitant.

Now, Sky Germany confirm that Krösche’s future likely lies in Italy because a move to Milan is becoming increasingly likely. However, no deal has been finalised yet: officials from both clubs still need to hold talks as Krösche is only on leave from Frankfurt.

His contract, which runs until 2028, is currently still valid. The 46-year-old insisted on having a release clause included in his contract. Specifically, this means that any club wanting to hire him before the summer of 2027 will have to pay a fee of approximately €5-7m, or negotiate with Eintracht.

No advanced talks have yet taken place, but Sky do add that Krösche is expected to take on the role of Head of Football with Milan. A start date of January 1, 2027 – coinciding with the start of the winter transfer window – is being discussed.

Meanwhile, Eintracht Frankfurt have already settled the question of Krösche’s successor. Joti Chatzialexiou is coming from 1. FC Nürnberg and will take over the position of sporting director. So, it seems like just a matter of time.

#1784. Sparta Prague 1-3 Bournemouth: Super subs complete comeback win

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Tyler Adams, Evanilson and Rayan all came off the bench to help Bournemouth come from behind to beat 10-man Sparta Prague 3-1 in the Europa League.

Ebrima Singhateh had given Sparta a first-half lead, just moments before Tobias Guddal was sent off, and Bournemouth rallied after the break to claim all three points at Epet Arena.

Jonathan Braut Brunes knocked a tap-in wide with just 70 seconds on the clock as Sparta immediately put Bournemouth on the back foot, though Lewis Cook soon fired wide at the other end.

Bournemouth had a golden opportunity to open the scoring from the penalty spot at the other end when Ki-Jana Hoover blocked David Brooks' shot with an outstretched arm, but when Lewis Cook stepped up, his low strike hit the foot of the left post before rolling along the goal line and out 28 minutes in.

Jakub Surovcik caught a tame Bafode Diakate header, and immediately set Sparta on the counter-attack, with his long clearance bouncing through to Singhateh, who drove through Bournemouth's half and skipped past two challenges to slot in after 35 minutes.

But just two minutes later, Guddal received his marching orders, having received a second booking for tugging back Alvaro Rodriguez.

Bournemouth pushed to make the most of their numerical advantage, and their pressure told in the 57th minute as Adams ran onto a loose ball to drill into the bottom-left corner.

The visitors continued to push, with Brooks and James Hill both kept out by Surovcik before Evanilson profited from loose defending. Santiago Eneme skipped past one challenge, but then lost out to Ryan Christie, who picked out the Brazilian to roll into the bottom-right corner after 81 minutes.

Rayan then capped the victory nine minutes later, winning back possession and playing a one-two with Evanilson before firing in a stunning long-range effort.

SEVEN WINS IN A ROW https://t.co/7GRhyUrGQa

— AFC Bournemouth  (@afcbournemouth) November 5, 2026

For all of Bournemouth's struggles at the start of the season, they are in stellar form after their busiest period of the campaign.

Marco Rose made eight changes to his starting XI for the third consecutive match and the fifth time in all competitions this season, but even with a sluggish start in Prague, they soon found their groove, helped by their substitutes.

Evanilson has scored six goals in his last seven games in all competitions, netting in three consecutive away matches for Bournemouth for the first time.

In total, the Cherries have scored five goals via substitutes in the Europa League this season, more than any other team. Adams, Evanilson and Rayan only had one shot apiece after their introductions, but they made them count.

Sparta certainly gave them issues in the first half before going down to 10 men, finishing the game with 12 shots worth 1.95 expected goals (xG) to Bournemouth's 20 attempts worth 2.3 xG.

But Bournemouth are on a roll having now won seven consecutive matches in all competitions for the first time since November 2014, when playing in England's second tier, and they look a fierce opposition no matter who they come up against.

#1783. Hibs boss insists his improving team are ready to upset the odds against Rangers in cup final

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER

Published: 14:00 EDT, 1 November 2026 | Updated: 15:31 EDT, 1 November 2026

Marink Reedijk warned Rangers that they'll face an ever-improving Hibs team when they meet in the Premier Sports Cup Final next month.

The Dutchman created history by becoming the first manager of the Easter Road club to taste a Hampden victory over Hearts when they came from behind to win 2-1.

After recording just one draw in his four opening league games, Reedijk was starting to feel the heat ahead of the semi-final.

But having secured a date against Rangers on December 13, the Leith boss feels his side are now in a different place.

Asked what gave him the confidence that his side can now upset the odds and win the cup for the first time since 2007, Reedijk said: 'The performance of today and the performance we showed the week before.

'And if we have more progression, we can make every opponent's lives a little bit difficult or very difficult.

Hibs boss Marink Reedijk celebrates his team's 2-1 win over Hearts with Josh Mulligan

'And no matter which team it is, it's always another match to play.

'Finals are, again, special matches, but also finals are not only based on these special moments.

'It's also about teams with a plan and teams with an idea.

'And I think if we build on what we are doing now, keep on going - it will have ups and downs - I know I have a really good belief that we also can do something in the final.'

Behind when Claudio Braga struck on four minutes, Hibs responded brilliantly and deservedly went in ahead at the break thanks to goals from Martin Boyle and Jamie McGrath.

Reedijk was effusive in his praise for the way his players bounced back from the early blow to dominate the game.

'In the first half, I really enjoyed how we played football, how we dominated the game on the ball, how we made sure that we created chances and gave Hearts a big problem in defence,' he reflected.

'And in the second half, I really enjoyed the togetherness, the work rate, the energy, the desire.

The Hibs players start the party after reaching League Cup final by beating Hearts

'This is where we made a big step today. And also I'm so happy for the staff, the players, because they worked so hard for this. And that's really important.

'Not only those people, like the staff and the players, but also for the fans who kept on supporting us, not only during the match, but especially those matches where we didn't have the result like it was today. And that's really important to me.

Reedijk was asked if his first victory at the fifth attempt was the first real sign that the players had bought into what he was trying to do.

'Not the first sign,' he stressed. 'For me, I already saw glimpses and signs in the last matches, starting at Falkirk, where you see that we dominated the game, but we didn't bring the game home and lost by individual errors and moments.

'And then against Celtic and St Mirren also you saw that we can dominate matches, that we can make our way of playing a challenge for the opponent. That didn't lead to the result we wanted.

'However, today it did. So, it is not the first sign, but it is the first performance with a result.'

Jamie McGrath soaks up the acclaim after putting Hibernian in front at Hampden

At full time, the entire Hibs squad lapped up the rendition of Sunshine on Leith which was sung by their supporters.

Reedijk admitted that he felt more emotional at the scenes than his impassive demeanour suggested.

'I'm not always showing my emotions, but it's really touching,' he said.

'Maybe it looks like I'm an ice king, so to say.

'Normally in Holland we say ice queen, but therefore an ice king because I'm not a woman.

'But for me, it is really important that this happens and it comes close to my heart because this is what football is about.

'Guys who inspire people on the pitch with something people off the pitch and in the stands love to see.

#1782. Cardiff City vs Burnley - prediction, team news, lineups

By Darren Plant | 05 Nov 2026 15:56

Cardiff City and Burnley square off on Saturday afternoon in what could prove to be a pivotal game in the battle to avoid relegation to League One.

While the Bluebirds sit in 18th position in the Championship table, Burnley are in 22nd spot, already four points adrift of safety.

With eight points from the last five games, Cardiff boss Brian Barry-Murphy can only be delighted with such a return.

The Bluebirds have played Watford, Middlesbrough, Birmingham City, Wolverhampton Wanderers and West Ham United in succession.

However, squandering a three-goal half-time lead against the latter of those teams would have hurt Barry-Murphy, regardless of West Ham benefitting from the arrival of new boss Scott Parker.

In the grand scheme of things, however, Cardiff are five points above the relegation zone and have put together a seven-match unbeaten run at the Cardiff City Stadium.

Trailing 12th place by just three points, the Welsh outfit are still in contention to launch a surprise playoff bid.

At the same time, defeat to Burnley on Saturday would see Cardiff only sit above the relegation zone by two points.

Fabio Celestini has got Burnley back on track with two respectable draws against Portsmouth and Queens Park Rangers.

While the well-travelled Italian knows that the Clarets need to deliver just a second Championship win of the season as soon as possible, there have at least been positives to take from his opening double header.

Burnley have collected five points from their last five away fixtures, arguably an encouraging return for a squad that has struggled to gel.

Nevertheless, if four results - including this one - go against them on Saturday, Burnley would end Saturday seven points adrift of safety.

With Cardiff right-back Perry Ng suffering an injury in the closing stages against West Ham, Ronan Kpakio is in line to deputise.

David Turnbull, Cian Ashford and Joel Colwill will all be considered for recalls due to the quick turnaround after the West Ham fixture.

Gabriel Osho, who has served a three-match ban, could get the nod over Will Fish in the middle of defence.

Barring any fresh injury concerns, Celestini may stick with the Burnley XI from the draw at QPR.

However, Josh Cullen, Aaron Ramsey and Jaydon Banel are all options in midfield and the final third.

Bashir Humphreys, Hannibal Mejbri and Chelsea loanee Dastan Satpaev remain on the sidelines.

Trott; Kpakio, Osho, Bagan, Scanlon; Robertson; Ashford, Moylan, J Colwill, Willock; Salech

Coudert; Walker; Ekdal, Julio, Pires; Hatate, Laurent; Hountondji, Edwards, Ramazini; Vardy

Having given up a three-goal lead against West Ham, it is anyone's guess how Cardiff will respond against Burnley. However, they deserve respect for the home record that they have compiled this campaign, leading us to predict a hard-earned victory for the Bluebirds.

#1780. Liverpool’s defensive errors ‘not sustainable’, says Van Dijk

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Virgil van Dijk insisted Liverpool's defence must improve, saying the errors they made in their Champions League defeat to Fenerbahce are "not sustainable".

Liverpool were beaten 3-2 at the Chobani Stadyumu Fenerbahce Sukru Saracoglu Spor Kompleksi, despite taking the lead twice on Tuesday.

Trey Nyoni's 25th-minute opener was swiftly cancelled out by Mason Greenwood, whose free-kick deflected in off Jeremy Jacquet after turning away from the ball in the wall.

Alexander Isak restored Liverpool's advantage three minutes after replacing Victor Munoz, but Fenerbahce responded once again when confusion from a set-piece saw Cody Gakpo flick the ball to the back post for Archie Brown to tuck home.

Fenerbahce completed the comeback in the 79th minute through Vedat Muriqi, who met Brown's looping cross with a towering header, despite being outnumbered by Jacquet, Nyoni and Alexis Mac Allister inside the penalty area.

The result saw Liverpool concede three goals from set pieces in a Champions League game for just the second time, along with their 3-3 draw with Sevilla in November 2017, though against Fenerbahce was the first time ever they have let in three non-penalty set-piece goals in one game.

Liverpool have also conceded 10 goals in four Champions League games this season, shipping three goals in each of their last three (6-3 vs LASK, 4-3 vs Villarreal, 2-3 vs Fenerbahce), the first time they have ever conceded 3+ goals in three major European games in a row.

"It's definitely not sustainable," said Van Dijk said of Liverpool's defensive woes.

"That's why it's very disappointing for many reasons, but definitely because of the goals we conceded and the manner we conceded them as well. There is work to do.

"Three set-pieces as well. We have been very good at them so far this season, but we switched off and weren't ready for the first and second balls. It's a tough one to take."

69 – Tonight was the latest Liverpool have ever taken the lead (69th minute – Alexander Isak to make it 2-1) in a major European match and then lost. Scuppered. https://t.co/OUAm9vxoyE

The defeat to Fenerbahce was only the third time in Liverpool's major European history they took the lead twice in a game and then lost, along with a 4-2 defeat to Roma in May 2018 and 3-2 defeat to PSV in January 2025.

And having gone ahead in the 69th minute, it was the latest Liverpool have ever taken the lead in a major European match and then lost.

Liverpool's defeat comes after they were beaten 1-0 by Arsenal in the Premier League, having won each of their last five matches across all competitions beforehand.

Andoni Iraola's side make the trip to Selhurst Park to face Crystal Palace on Sunday, though Van Dijk believes their midweek experience will only be beneficial for the Liverpool players as they look to sign off for the international break with a positive result.

"I mentioned after the last game [against Arsenal] that we as a group have to go through good moments but also less good moments," Van Dijk added.

"That will only form a bigger bond and it will only be beneficial. No-one wants to lose games, especially as we did, but it should only help us in the near future.

"We should not accept losing, especially in the manner we did."

#1779. Bristol City vs Norwich City - prediction, team news, lineups

By Calum Burrowes | 05 Nov 2026 15:57, Last updated: 05 Nov 2026 16:04

In desperate need of positive results, Bristol City welcome Norwich City to Ashton Gate on Saturday afternoon for a Championship clash.

The Robins suffered their third defeat in five matches on Wednesday, losing 2-1 to Wolverhampton Wanderers, while the Canaries continued their winning streak with a thumping 4-0 victory over Derby County at Pride Park.

There was plenty of optimism surrounding Bristol City following the appointment of Michael Skubala and the investment made during what appeared to be a productive transfer window, but 15 games into his tenure, the former Lincoln City boss is already under pressure and could find his position under threat if results do not improve in the coming weeks.

The early signs at the end of August and start of September were encouraging, with the Robins collecting nine points from a possible nine across a seven-day spell against Portsmouth, Preston North End and Burnley.

However, the South West side have won just twice since then, slipping out of the playoff places and into the bottom half of the table.

Scott Twine's 93rd-minute winner against Bolton Wanderers on Halloween lifted the mood around Ashton Gate, and Bristol City appeared on course to make it back-to-back victories when they entered the final 10 minutes against Wolves with their lead intact, only for a seven-minute brace from Sean Neave to turn the game on its head and condemn Skubala to yet another disappointing result.

Bristol City's main concerns have been their lack of attacking threat and continued struggles at home, with only four sides scoring fewer than the Robins' 16 goals this season and just two teams winning fewer than their two matches at Ashton Gate.

Their attacking problems are clearly a concern for Skubala, who switched to a two-striker system against Stoke City and Bolton Wanderers before reverting to a lone forward for the midweek defeat.

Norwich City, meanwhile, make the trip from East Anglia to Bristol in buoyant spirits, having enjoyed a dramatic turnaround in form that has significantly improved their position in the Championship table following three successive victories.

Wins over Charlton Athletic, Watford and, most recently, Derby County have helped Philippe Clement's side climb from 21st to 12th, leaving them closer to the playoff places than the relegation zone.

The Canaries secured their latest three points in emphatic fashion, travelling to Pride Park in good form and facing a Derby side who had not won since early September.

First-half goals from Anthony Musaba, Paris Maghoma and Darlin Yongwa put Norwich firmly in control before substitute Jovon Makamba came off the bench to add a superb fourth.

Before this winning run, Norwich had scored just twice in their previous 270 minutes of football, but Clement's men have since enjoyed a remarkable upturn in front of goal, finding the net 10 times across their last three matches, with their first clean providing another timely boost.

It was the Canaries' first clean sheet in 24 matches, although their defensive record remains a concern with 24 goals conceded in 14 Championship outings, a total bettered by only a handful of sides, while their recent scoring spree has lifted them to the point where only three teams have a stronger attacking record.

Both teams head into Saturday's encounter level on points and could finish the weekend just one point outside the playoff places.

Although Bristol City came through their midweek encounter without any fresh injury concerns, Skubala still has a number of selection decisions to make.

New signing Sam Tickle was recently dropped in favour of Brad Collins in goal, with the Chelsea academy product starting the last three matches.

However, Collins was at fault for both goals against Wolves and could now find himself relegated to the bench.

Lorent Tolaj was forced off with an injury during the Robins' goalless draw with Stoke City last month and is expected to return in the coming weeks, meaning Saturday's encounter is likely to come too soon for the forward.

Twine, who scored a superb first-half free kick against Wolves, is expected to retain his place in the starting lineup.

Having overseen their best run of the season, Clement will be keen to maintain Norwich's winning momentum for the trip to the South West.

Maghoma and Musaba have scored five goals between them across the last three matches and are expected to feature again in attack, while Mathias Kvistgaarden will continue to lead the line in the absence of Mohamed Toure.

Papa Amadou Diallo and Ali Ahmed remain the only other players unavailable for the Canaries.

Collins; Tanner, McNally, Eissat, Pring; Knight, Williams; Cardines, Tolaj, Twine; Ballard

Grimshaw; Stacey, Darling, McCoville, Yongwa; Wright, Field; Musaba, Maghoma, Brooks; Kvistgaarden

Both sides head into this encounter level on points but in contrasting form, with Norwich enjoying a three-match winning streak while Bristol City have struggled for consistency.

Nevertheless, the Robins are due a positive result on home soil, and we expect them to end their recent struggles with a closely fought victory on Saturday.

#1778. Hearts boss Wouter Vrancken says the loss of two more players to injury was costly in semi-final defeat

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER

Published: 15:31 EDT, 1 November 2026 | Updated: 15:31 EDT, 1 November 2026

Wouter Vrancken claimed Hearts were unable to cope with the double blow of losing Tomas Magnusson and Calvin Miller as their hopes of lifting the Premier Sports Cup ended with a 2-1 defeat by Hibs.

Already missing eight first-team players, the Tynecastle men were further depleted when the pair left the field inside the opening 38 minutes of their semi-final at Hampden.

Vrancken felt the loss of two more key players was instrumental in his side failing to build on the early lead handed to them by Claudio Braga.

Instead, Hibs hit back with goals by Martin Boyle and Jamie McGrath to secure a place in next month's final against Rangers.

'I'm really sore and disappointed, of course, especially when you see how the game was going,' said Vrancken.

'It didn't have to go that way because we had control with how we started.

Wouter Vrancken insists Hearts had control until two key players left the field with injuries

Tomas Magnusson is treated for a head knock that led to his substitution early in the semi-final

Calvin Miller uses crutches after going off with what appeared to be a knee injury at Hampden

'But it changed the moment Tomas was injured, that's clear. And then afterwards with Cal.

'I'm not pointing out the guys who came out, but those changes took us out of our rhythm.

'We lost some connections and weren't top in the duels. At first, we were picking up second balls and finding the right spaces.

'But then we lost those profiles and we were searching again. There were hesitations and that gave Hibs too much space.

'You lose the game in that 20 minutes. At half-time, we tried to make adjustments, be clear and try to take those hesitations out.

'It was much better and we dominated the game again.

'Unfortunately, we didn't get rewarded. The players have taken a lot of knocks mentally and emotionally so you just hope they get rewarded for fighting hard.

'It's a pity they didn't especially in such a game.'

Magnusson came off with a head-knock while Miller succumbed to what appeared to be a knee injury.

'I haven't seen Tomas because he's at hospital,' Vrancken explained.

'Calvin is in a brace, but it's difficult to say. We have to wait for a scan tomorrow.

'With Tomas, the medical staff did a concussion test on the pitch at that moment.

'He passed it but when he came to me, he was going from left to right and couldn't stand on his legs any more.

'When I saw that, there was no doubt in my head about letting him back on the pitch. He said, I can't do it.'

Vrancken now faces serious selection issues for the Conference League match away to Swiss side Thun on Thursday.

'I don't know how I make changes. We'll see how it goes and who's fit,' he said.

'Players will have to play out of position, so we'll see who has the quality to play in certain ones.

'We have to make the puzzle on Monday or Tuesday.

'And we have to keep pushing the guys because when you go on the pitch, there can be no excuses, you have to take responsibility, go for it and try to win the game.

'We have 10 out. When you have those 10, you have a really good squad in the Premiership.

'The players have taken responsibility in difficult moments, like dominating parts of the game today.

'When they do that, you just hope they reward themselves like they did today in the second half. It's just a pity the last 20 minutes of the first half which killed the game.

'Everyone is disappointed, no matter the situation we're in.

'When you see the second half, you know there was something in the game today even with the knocks we got.

'So, the disappointment is really big, not about losing players, but missing the chance to beat your rivals and go to the final.'

#1777. Toronto playing for pride after missing out on playoffs

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Despite missing out on an MLS playoff spot, Robin Fraser says Toronto FC are playing for pride when they travel to the Philadelphia Union on Decision Day.

Toronto sit 12th in the Eastern Conference with 39 points, four behind ninth-place Orlando City SC, with their 3-1 loss to Atlanta United last weekend ending their outside hopes of reaching the playoffs.

The Reds had given themselves hope, losing just one of their five games prior to the Atlanta defeat, but they now know their season will be coming to an end on Saturday.

Fraser was disappointed with the outcome of their campaign, but he is still determined to make sure they finish the regular season on a high.

"Obviously, people are let down," said Fraser. "But I do think that from what we've seen, this pride factor is an important thing.

"There are guys who have different things to play for – whether it's contracts or longevity or starting positions – there's always something to play for, I think, as a professional.

"Of course, we want to finish on a good note. First and foremost is to win the game. We want to do all things the right way.

"If you're a professional, I feel like that should be your obligation. There's no other thought."

— Toronto FC (@TorontoFC) November 4, 2026

Philadelphia's postseason place is already confirmed as they sit sixth in the East, but a poor result this weekend could see them drop out of the automatic places into one of the wildcard spots.

After storming back into the playoff picture with stunning form after the World Cup break, the Union have slipped at the wrong time, failing to win any of their last four league games (D2 L2), including a 1-0 loss to FC Cincinnati last time out.

And ahead of Decision Day, club captain Alejandro Bedoya has revealed he will be retiring at the end of the 2026 season, after 11 seasons at the club.

"When I look back on my time in Philadelphia, so many moments come to mind, from the big wins and incredible matches to the challenges we faced along the way," said Bedoya.

"However, what stands out most is everything beyond the game. I came here because I believed in what the club was building and wanted to be part of that vision. Over time, Philadelphia became so much more than the place I came to play soccer.

"I'll miss this city and this club tremendously, but I take comfort in knowing I've given everything I had on the pitch.

"Philadelphia and this club have given me more than I ever could have imagined when I first arrived, and I'll always be grateful for that."

A resurgent Tottenham Hotspur side travel to Elland Road to take on an out-of-sorts Leeds United outfit in the Premier League on Saturday lunchtime.

The spoils were shared the last time these two teams butted heads in May, with Mathys Tel’s opener cancelled out by a Dominic Calvert-Lewin penalty to rescue a 1-1 draw in North London.

After making a bright start to the season, accumulating eight points from their opening four games (W2 D2), Leeds are now without a win across their last five matches (D3 L2) and have slipped down to 12th in the Premier League table.

The Whites continue to stumble after a 2-0 defeat against Bournemouth, adding to a rough patch that includes a 2-1 loss at champions Arsenal alongside draws with struggling trio Crystal Palace, Manchester United and Sunderland.

Head coach Daniel Farke – who reached an agreement in principle over a contract extension last month – has downplayed concerns over Leeds' recent winless streak, maintaining that his squad remains calm and confident while prioritising reaching the 40-point safety mark as quickly as possible.

Leeds should welcome a return to Elland Road where they are unbeaten across their last eight league matches (W4 D4); they are one of only four Premier League teams yet to lose on home soil so far this season along with Arsenal, Brighton and Hull.

However, the Whites have collected only five points across their last 13 top-flight battles with Spurs, losing 10 of those, while they have failed to keep a clean sheet in any of their last 16 encounters with the North Londoners – a 1-0 home win back in February 2000 was the last time Leeds did not concede against Spurs.

After enduring a six-game winless start to the Premier League, Tottenham’s early-season struggles now seem to be behind them as Roberto De Zerbi has steered his team to three consecutive victories against Coventry, Chelsea and Crystal Palace.

Spurs opened their account with a 3-1 home win over Coventry just under a fortnight ago and have since recorded back-to-back 2-0 successes against Chelsea and Palace, beating the latter last weekend after taking advantage of a 13th-minute red card for Eagles striker Jean-Philippe Mateta.

The North Londoners have risen up to ninth place in the Premier League table, just two points behind the top five and crucially five points clear of the bottom three; they are now bidding to win four league games in a row for the first time since September and October 2023.

De Zerbi has encouraged his players to build on their positive upturn in form, as three straight wins is “not enough” to please the supporters. The Italian also hopes to see a ‘nastier’ side from his attacking players in front of goal after scoring only two goals from 34 shots against Palace.

Spurs head into Saturday’s contest with Leeds seeking to extend their three-game unbeaten away run in the top flight, while they have won each of their last three visits to Elland Road by an aggregate score of 10-2.

Leeds duo Noah Okafor (adductor) and Anton Stach (broken toe) remain major doubts, while Farke "carefully optimistic" that striker Dominic Calvert-Lewin – who has scored seven goals in his last seven home games – will be fit after missing training on Thursday with a foot problem.

Former Spurs defender Joe Rodon is back in full training and in contention to return to the matchday squad after missing the last eight games in all competitions with a hamstring injury. A start is considered unlikely, though, so James Justin, Nico Elvedi and Tarik Muharemovic should all continue in the back three.

James Trafford will "remain in goal" despite his costly mistake in the defeat at Bournemouth, while Lukas Nmecha, Brenden Aaronson and Jean-Matteo Bahoya are three attackers who could be considered for a start should Farke look to shake up his attack.

As for Tottenham, Wilson Odobert (knee), Mykhaylo Mudryk (ankle) and Xavi Simons (ACL) all remain out, though the latter is making positive progress in his recovery and could return soon than expected.

Savio (muscle) is believed to have returned to training this week and it remains to be seen whether the winger will be fit to return to the matchday squad, while Lucas Bergvall (knee) and Tosin Adarabioyo (calf) are both minor doubts.

De Zerbi may look to make only two changes to his starting lineup, with Pedro Porro pushing to replace Archie Gray at right-back, while playmaker James Maddison could start at the expense of either Omar Marmoush or Dominic Solanke who are both battling for the centre-forward spot.
