#1773. Alexander Isak starts to justify £125m price tag with double

There was a centre-forward who played for Newcastle a couple of years ago. Do you remember him? He was as quick as greased lightning, played on his instincts, had a shot like cannon and could come up with a finish for every situation.

Everyone wanted him, but Liverpool signed him for £125m in August 2025. His name was Alexander Isak but shortly after arriving on Merseyside, it was like he went missing, as the guy who played in red last season bore only a physical resemblance to the guy who had played in black-and-white.

If you had wondered what had happened to him, he reappeared at Portman Road. They say good things come to those who wait. Although nobody at Liverpool would have expected such a delay to see the real Isak, there were no complaints that his career at the club has finally taken off.

Taking the headlines from Bradley Barcola on a big night at Portman Road was going to take some doing, but Isak did just that with a double salvo in the opening nine minutes, a flurry so potent it was like a boxer charging out of their corner and seeing the first blows land flush on their opponent’s jaw.

Poor Ipswich. There is universal recognition that Liverpool are a team – and a club – in transition but they had four players in Isak, Florian Wirtz, Cody Gakpo and Victor Muñoz who had the potential to dismantle the hosts if they clicked and that is precisely what happened.

“With Alex, it is clear,” said Andoni Iraola. “If he is fit, if he is available, if he is in a good shape, he will produce the numbers. My demand with Alex will not be about the goals. It will be about other things so we can play well. And if we play well, we are in good positions. Then goals will come.”

So for all the noisy backing they received from the stands and for all the effort Gary O’Neil’s side put into a contest that TV companies had chosen to broadcast because there was a potential for drama, Isak blew a hole in Ipswich’s hull in the sixth minute and they were submerging from there on in.

A blistering finish from Alexander Isak! 💥 pic.twitter.com/jSGlIZsQtA

How Isak, who had scored against Nottingham Forest last weekend, needed a night like this when he made a genuine difference. But the same was true, too, for Iraola. We live in an era where someone has to be in the eye of a storm and the Basque will know what comes with his new territory.

It had clearly irritated Iraola that Liverpool had gone behind four times in their opening two fixtures and during his pre-match media briefing, he effectively gave a sermon at one point on how slow starts, or giving the opposition a helping hand, would no longer be tolerated.

Quietly, Iraola is making his presence felt. The task he faces is significantly different than the one O’Neil is accomplishing – keeping Ipswich in the division against the odds – but Liverpool’s head coach is a man who knows his own mind and is not afraid to make decisions.

He had responded to criticism of his midfield at Newcastle on the opening weekend by dropping Ryan Gravenberch for the fixture with Forest and his response to scrutiny about his right-back seven days ago was to drop Jeremie Frimpong and bring in Ronald Araújo.

Iraola certainly picked the right team: Araújo, the loan capture from Barcelona, added stature to the back four and there was harmony in how they moved. The Uruguayan’s first instinct was to stay back and Liverpool looked better for it, even if O’Neil, incredibly, felt Ipswich had the better of things.

Emersonn, Ipswich’s Brazilian striker, did not see the ball in the opening exchanges and, by the time he did, Liverpool had zoomed into the distance to such an extent that you felt it was going to be impossible for them to peg their visitors back.

“I hate having to talk about good performances when you do not get points,” O’Neil declared to a room full of raised eyebrows and you can only assume his message was to ensure that morale in the dressing room was not drooping.

What damage was inflicted with Liverpool’s first significant attack. Gakpo, the subject of an £80m bid from Manchester City, was never going to allow transfer speculation to disrupt his focus and he nudged a perfect little ball into Isak’s path in the sixth minute to show his wellbeing.

The next move announced the return of Isak. One touch gave him an avenue to shoot, the next was a shot with his right foot that was so hard from 16 yards, on an angle, it bent the wrists of Kjell Scherpen as it howled into the net. Critics will feel Ipswich’s keeper should have done better.

Your first thought was to think of the first goal Isak scored in English football in September 2022, a similarly venomous drive, against Liverpool at Anfield. He oozed quality that evening, his pace and skill had Jürgen Klopp’s defenders persistently fretting and this is what he was doing again.

It was no coincidence that three minutes later, he came up with another wonderful goal. This one owed much to the beautiful pass Gakpo presented to him, an inch-perfect through ball with the outside of his right foot, but Isak still showed great poise to bamboozle Scherpen.

Inside NINE minutes Alexander Isak has two goals! ⚡️ pic.twitter.com/3UGq0bwqRm

“He owes me a few assists now!” chirped the selfless Gakpo.

A hat-trick could have arrived in the 32nd minute but Isak was a kneecap offside as he dispatched a pass from Wirtz and, perhaps, he will have been disappointed to have made way on the hour having not secured the match ball for his efforts.

Liverpool, too, will be frustrated that they did not made sure of three points before the time Isak made way for Barcola – what Alexis Mac Alliser was thinking when he fluffed an unmarked header from six yards, only he will know – but it was not a night to nitpick.

There will be easier assignments on the horizon for Ipswich, even though O’Neil insisted they more than held their own against world-class opponents. And you can say for sure there will be more goals and wins for Liverpool and Isak if they continue in this encouraging manner.

“I witnessed what a great coach he was at Bournemouth. He is not the sort of manager you are going to see making clever patterns in his box. He just does not see the risk. He will want to get the ball to the players who want to make a difference. Coaches do not show how good they are by how they play out from the back. The important thing is when you get it in the final third, you make things happen. That is what he will want to improve. He will want Alexander Isak when he has not got the ball to press. He will want the same of Florian Wirtz. The difficulty will come with Champions League football and not putting too many demands on his players. If he gets it right, he has got a wonderful squad to work with.”

"My demands will not be about the goals, my fights with him are about other stuff." Andoni Iraola speaking about Alexander Isak 🔊 pic.twitter.com/B4zUG2IGfS

“He has had good minutes, a good pass in a counter, a good couple of chances when he was going against the goalkeeper and we have not found him. We need to learn these movements because he will be there threatening in behind all the team. But he looks confident on the ball as always. He had not played any competitive minutes since the World Cup so we had to be a little bit more careful.”

"Yeah, that's nice" 😁Alexander Isak talks through his second goal vs Ipswich 🔍 pic.twitter.com/diG2xv50Bw

“We were waiting for the first win, and we were talking about starting the game well, which we have not done recently. And we did that with two goals. With a normal pre-season, I think we are starting to get the way we want to play, being offensive and attack the defence. We showed that today. We scored two and could have scored more.

“It was not easy. It was a long injury, a difficult season [last season] in general. I was thinking; I want to have a good World Cup firstly and then to start the season well, which I feel like I have done now. That season is kind of behind me, but it was not easy.”

The first half is brought to an end at Portman Road and Isak’s quickfire double early in the half gives Liverpool a 2-0 lead at the break.

Isak has the ball in the Ipswich net for the third time tonight and thinks he has his hat-trick but the offside flag goes up. It comes from a stunning piece of play from Wirtz down Liverpool’s left, taking up a pocket of space and taking the ball on the turn beautifully. He then spots Isak in space at the far post and picks him out perfectly, with Isak slotting home. However, the offside flag is up and replays prove he was just offside. Could Isak have timed his run just fractionally better and still reached the cross? Probably but it was very close.

And there he is. You have been waiting 12 months to see the Alexander Isak of Newcastle play for Liverpool but here he is, a confident, instinctive-finishing menace. His first goal was marvellous, his second was a work of art, given the pass from Cody Gakpo, and what a position Liverpool have put themselves in to get their first win under Andoni Iraola. And, while we are at it, Gakpo has made both Liverpool’s goals: what on earth were they doing thinking of selling him to Manchester City?

Isak, on his last trip to Portman Road, scored a hat-trick for Newcastle here in a 4-0 win back in December 2024. He already has two goals to his name tonight inside the opening quarter of an hour.

Emersonn misses from close range for Ipswich but the offside flag goes up against Greaves. It was a bad miss from Emersonn but Greaves, who had delivered the cross for Emersonn, was offside.

We are about to find out the two starting XIs at Portman Road. Will Bradley Barcola start for Liverpool on his debut?

The third matchday of the new Premier League season kicks off at Portman Road as newly-promoted Ipswich host Liverpool.

Andoni Iraola has drawn his first two games in charge of Liverpool, both 2-2 stalemates against Newcastle and Nottingham Forest respectively. Liverpool secured a move for forward Bradley Barcola from PSG in the final few days on the window for a fee that could rise to £123m and the Frenchman is set to make his Liverpool debut tonight.

“We are very happy with Bradley,” Iraola said. “He was our priority; to sign a very good player in that position. He has come with the right mentality. I like that he wanted Liverpool a lot, he just wanted to come here. That is a good first sign. Being the player he is and the things he has won recently, he has come with the willingness to help us. I am very happy with him.

“He trained well with us, and if everything goes well in today’s [Thursday] training, he will definitely be available for tomorrow [tonight]. He has trained with us three times. He has not had minutes in pre-season but he has been training normally with the group. It is a decision we have to make. We have to consider that he has not had minutes in pre-season.”

Liverpool won both fixtures when Ipswich were last in the Premier League two seasons ago, including a 2-0 win on the opening weekend in Arne Slot’s first game in charge of Liverpool as they went on to win the Premier League that season.

Ipswich won their first home game on their return to the Premier League, beating Sunderland 2-1 on the opening weekend. However, they fell to a 5-2 defeat in their first away game at Manchester United. Over the course of the summer transfer window, Ipswich made a total of 14 signings and spent over £200m.

“What we can do is perform in a way that always gives us a real chance, which we have done so far,” Ipswich boss Gary O’Neil said. “We were in that game at Manchester United until a couple of moments took it away from us. We were in it, so that is what we need to do, we need to make sure that no matter who it is, whether it is Liverpool, Manchester United, Manchester City, when they come to Portman Road, we need to make sure we are right in the game to give ourselves opportunities. We will always be a threat; we have scored four goals in two games. That is really good for a promoted side. We look a goal threat, and we need to keep that going and that will be tested.”

#1772. GdS: Necessities, dreams and surprises – the January mercato Milan have in mind

AC Milan owner Gerry Cardinale is ready to do what is possible to strengthen the squad when the window reopens.

La Gazzetta dello Sport report that the Milan owner is passionate, so while he got emotional after the derby win against Inter, he was also worried following the defeat to Bologna and the limitations it exposed. So, he is ready to give Ruben Amorim a helping hand, but where?

Amorim said that, with the squad reduced by injuries, it’s difficult to press hard and play the football he prefers. We didn’t see that in the derby, but that’s another story.

Koni De Winter and Strahinja Pavlovic are the defenders who could use a union representative: they always play, never rest, and almost never come out early. Mario Gila is the other starter, but then Fikayo Tomori and Matteo Gabbia – the natural back-ups – are injured.

That leaves Filippo Terracciano and Sankhoun Diawara, who are more uncertainties than guarantees at present. A signing will arrive and Sporting CP’s Gonçalo Inacio was the target in the summer. The asking price was €40m then, and the Rossoneri could offer it again.

The striker issue is a different story. Milan invested over €70m in Gonçalo Ramos this summer, a deal that is now viewed with some trepidation. It’s right to give Ramos time, but Cardinale has recently fallen head over heels for Nicolò Tresoldi, who scored a hat-trick against Inter in the Champions League.

Tresoldi has been a Milan fan since childhood and doesn’t hide it. Milan would gladly give him the satisfaction of playing for the Rossoneri, but Club Brugge wanted €50m in the summer and it could be more now. Moreover, the De Ketelaere and Jashari negotiations show how difficult they are to deal with.

Will there be any other surprises? A wing-back is possible if Amorim decides the left side needs more momentum, or Samuel Chukwueze finds some company  in the treatment room. A goalkeeper to give Lorenzo Torriani a loan chance is possible. With Cardinale, nothing can be ruled out.

#1771. Virgil van Dijk and Andoni Iraola hit out after Liverpool denied 'clear penalty' against Arsenal - as Reds boss reveals he will tell Alexander Isak to 'dive on floor' in future

By BEN WILLCOCKS, ASSISTANT SPORTS EDITOR and LEWIS STEELE, FOOTBALL REPORTER

Published: 14:45 EDT, 1 November 2026 | Updated: 17:17 EDT, 1 November 2026

Andoni Iraola has revealed he will now tell Alexander Isak to 'dive on the floor' as he and Virgil van Dijk hit out at VAR after Liverpool were denied a 'clear penalty' during Sunday's 1-0 defeat by Arsenal.

The Gunners ended their 14-year wait for a Premier League victory at Anfield to return to the top of the table, keeping Liverpool at bay with a superb defensive performance after Kai Havertz opened the scoring in the 16th minute.

Just minutes after the German's opener, Liverpool striker Isak looked to have a golden opportunity to equalise when he rose to meet Bradley Barcola's cross, only to miss the ball after having his shirt pulled back by Arsenal defender Jurrien Timber.

Despite clearly tugging the Swede's shirt, Timber escaped punishment from referee Andy Madley, while VAR opted not to intervene and award Liverpool a penalty despite protests from Iraola and his players.

Sky Sports pundits Jamie Carragher, Daniel Sturridge and Ian Wright unanimously agreed Liverpool should have been awarded a penalty at half-time and suggested that Isak was denied the spot-kick because he failed to make more of the incident.

Andoni Iraola (right) and Virgil van Dijk (left) hit out at VAR after Liverpool were denied a 'clear penalty' during Arsenal's 1-0 win at Anfield on Sunday

Alexander Isak was blatantly pulled back by Jurrien Timber but was not awarded a penalty

Iraola thinks the game could have gone differently had Madley not missed Timber's shirt pull.

The Liverpool boss said after the match: ‘There are two situations and they are a little bit related. The Isak one is a clear penalty.

‘He's gonna head the ball in front of the goal, and they grab him where everyone sees the shirt. You don't need a lot, just to avoid Alex, because the ball just goes in front of him, and I don't see the reason why, probably because he doesn't dive or he doesn't go to the floor. It shouldn't be a reason not to concede a penalty.

Iraola also pointed to a similar situation where Cody Gakpo was tugged back, but the officials said the Dutchman would not get to the ball.

‘They say the ball was too long and Cody wouldn't have arrived to the ball, but then you're basically accepting that the first one is, is a pen, no?’ added Iraola. ‘So you cannot use the argument in both ways differently. So I think it's a, yes, it's a pen, the Alex one is.’

Speaking to Sky Sports after the match, the manager said: 'It's a problem we have with the game. Because he doesn't dive and go to the floor. The fact that you are even asking me if he should go to the floor, if he goes to the floor, they call the penalty 100 per cent.

'It should be like this but it is what it is. Next time, the managers should tell Alex to go to the floor, otherwise they won't call it.'

Van Dijk insisted it should not be on his team-mate Isak to make more of the incident

Asked if he will tell Isak to do that in future, the Spaniard replied: 'Yes, definitely.'

Reds captain Virgil van Dijk took aim at VAR too after the match, expressing his disappointment at the defeat.

'I think it was a clear penalty. I've seen it back and I've seen it being given. Today it wasn't meant to be,' he said.

Asked if Isak should have reacted more, the Dutchman added: 'We have 50 cameras. Why does he have to complain when there are so many cameras?

'Everyone has seen it. In the end it wasn't given and we lose the game unfortunately, so well done to Arsenal.'

Former Liverpool defender Carragher was furious that VAR had not intervened as he analysed the incident at half-time.

'One of the best goal-scorers in the league is pulled back seven yards from goal, and the pull back stops him heading the ball. Why does he need to make a meal of it? VAR, do your job,' he said bluntly.

Arsenal moved to the top of the table on 24 points with victory at Anfield, while Liverpool remained fifth after Brighton and Chelsea, who are third and fourth respectively, both won on Saturday.

Mikel Arteta hailed his side’s resilience to win at Anfield.

Asked if it feels better to do so as a player or manager, he said: ‘Now it feels better as a manager, it has been such a long time without this feeling. We are extremely proud, especially the conditions we arrived in after the defeat against Fleetwood looked like the end of the world.

‘But then you have to pick yourself up. Four days later you have to come to Anfield against this manager and this team.’

#1770. Maresca not concerned by Donnarumma’s recent mistakes

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Enzo Maresca insists he has no concerns over Gianluigi Donnarumma's recent form, giving the goalkeeper his full backing ahead of their Premier League trip to Nottingham Forest.

Donnarumma was at fault for one of the goals City conceded in their 3-2 win over RB Leipzig in the Champions League on Wednesday, as he was beaten at the near post by Ridle Baku.

Across all competitions this season, Donnarumma has made three errors leading to goals – with one of those coming against Aston Villa in a loss that ended City's perfect start to the Premier League campaign.

City have lost their last two league matches, slipping to second in the table behind Arsenal, but Maresca has no doubt that Donnarumma will get back to his best soon.

"It's not a concern, but it's a mistake," Maresca said when asked about Donnarumma.

"We recognise that; he knows that it's a mistake, but now it's Nottingham Forest away, we need to be focused on that."

Asked if he was thinking of reviewing the position during the international break, Maresca told a press conference: "I'm not, to be honest. Seriously, at the moment I'm not thinking about the international break and goalkeeper situation because we are talking about a mistake.

"A few minutes before the mistake, he has made a save that any keeper in the world is not going to do. So, it's always a balance.

"Gigio knows that the first goal was not good, but, again, he's going to do better."

What a stop, Gigio! https://t.co/wBAIFIrooD

— Manchester City (@ManCity) November 5, 2026

Forest are struggling at the other end of the table, sitting in 19th coming into the weekend, with only one win to their name in the league so far (D3 L5).

Their winless streak stretched to five games after going down 2-0 to Brentford last time out, a result which prompted an impassioned rant from Oliver Glasner, who said the team needed to make changes.

He even went as far as to say, "If you don't want to follow, then I guess the sixth manager will come in", hinting at Forest's many changes in the dugout since the start of last season.

But Glasner believes that warning has had the desired impact on his players.

"I didn't attack anyone directly. We share that we want to be successful and win games. It was not a problem," he said.

"It was much louder outside than I felt it was inside. This is just how I see a relationship has to be. Let's talk about things if we don't like things.

"I can't blame somebody because if they don't know, how can you expect things to change?

"We are now in a society where criticism or the way I talk is negative, but the intention was positive and to change to get better results so that we can all have a better life."

Morgan Gibbs-White could make his 200th Premier League appearance in this match.

Of the 199 so far, 151 have been for Nottingham Forest, the third-most for the club in the competition.

Back at the City Ground on Saturday. https://t.co/X7GxOpQ0GH

— Nottingham Forest (@NFFC) November 4, 2026

Elliot Anderson has made more passes while under high pressure than any other player in the Premier League this season (357), and he will be determined to make an impact on his return to his former side.

Forest have won one of their last nine Premier League games against City (D3 L5), a 1-0 home win in the 2024-25 season.

City, meanwhile, are looking to record consecutive away top-flight wins at Forest for the first time since January 1925.

The Citizens have lost their last two Premier League games, though, as many as they had in their previous 33 (W23 D8). Only once in the last 10 years have they lost more consecutively, losing four in a row in November/December 2024.

Having become the 10th team in English top-flight history to win each of their first seven games in a campaign, City have now lost their last two. Only Sheffield Wednesday in 1904-05 have won their first seven and then lost their next three.

But Forest are on a more worrying run. They are winless in their last six Premier League home games (D3 L3), failing to score in each of their last four.

Only twice have they had a longer run without a home league goal – six games between November 2011/January 2012 and five games between December 2017/February 2018.

#1769. Man Utd transfer news: Red Devils 'tempting' Premier League defender with Old Trafford move

By Carter White | 05 Nov 2026 16:02, Last updated: 05 Nov 2026 20:47

Manchester United have reportedly set their sights on Fulham defender Calvin Bassey ahead of the January transfer window.

Michael Carrick's men ended their worrying winless run on Tuesday night, when a Matheus Cunha brace helped the Red Devils come from two goals down to secure a 3-2 victory over Roma in the Champions League.

Absent from the Theatre of Dreams earlier in the week, Man Utd wonderkid JJ Gabriel is heading towards a switch away from England, with European giants Real Madrid keen on the teenager.

Despite their comeback success over the Italians on Tuesday, the Red Devils and head coach Carrick are still under an enormous amount of pressure given their wretched form in the top flight.

Man Utd have won just one of their opening nine top-flight contests of the 2026-27 campaign - their worst start in over four decades - leaving them 17th in the Premier League standings, level on points with the relegation zone.

According to Football Insider, Manchester United are desperate to make improvements in defensive areas during the January transfer window after conceding at a rate of knots so far this campaign.

The report states that the Red Devils are hoping to sign a new left-footed central defender, given that Lisandro Martinez's time at Old Trafford is seemingly drawing towards a toxic conclusion.

As a result, it is understood that Carrick's troops are eyeing up a New Year swoop for Bassey, who has been one of the standout performers for Fulham amid a difficult start to the term for the Cottagers.

Despite the mess at the Theatre of Dreams at present, it is believed that the Nigeria international could be tempted by a switch to Man Utd if they pushed for his signature in January.

Bassey's current contract at Craven Cottage expires at the conclusion of the 2026-27 season, however, Fulham can extend those terms by a further 12 months - an option that is likely to be triggered imminently.

After bolstering heavily in their attacking and midfield ranks in the summers of 2025 and 2026 respectively, Manchester United are now on a mission to bring defensive stability back to Old Trafford.

The Red Devils are relying on a host of long-serving assets at the moment, with Harry Maguire, Luke Shaw and Diogo Dalot all going through periods of struggle with the team in recent years.

At 26 years of age, Bassey is entering the prime of his professional career and would be a much-needed breath of fresh air for Man Utd, who are in danger of being involved in a relegation scrap this season.

#1767. Prediction: Valencia vs Real Madrid

Real Madrid continue their pursuit of the La Liga summit on Saturday evening when they travel to Mestalla to take on Valencia.

Jose Mourinho’s side arrive in excellent form, having won seven consecutive matches in all competitions, while Valencia are hoping recent signs of improvement can help them climb away from the relegation zone.

Valencia’s season has been a struggle from the outset.

Los Che sit 19th in the standings with just nine points from 11 league matches and boast one of the weakest attacking records in the division, having scored only eight goals all season. Those numbers underline the scale of the challenge facing Javier Aguirre as he attempts to steer the club away from danger.

There was at least a welcome boost before the international break, as Umar Sadiq’s goal secured a vital 1-0 victory away to Elche. The success ended a difficult run and offered supporters hope that results may finally be turning in the right direction.

Now, Valencia have the opportunity to record back-to-back league victories for the first time since last season, although few opponents provide a sterner test than Real Madrid.

Sergi Canos, Diego Lopez and David Otorbi are unavailable, while Jose Manuel Copete faces a late fitness assessment.

The return of Sadiq, however, comes at an important time. After scoring the winner against Elche, the striker is expected to return to the starting lineup, while Harvey Elliott is available again following suspension.

Real Madrid head to the east coast as one of Europe’s form teams.

Mourinho’s side made it seven straight victories in all competitions with a dramatic 3-2 Champions League success away to AEK Athens in midweek. That result continued a remarkable run that has also included victories over Barcelona, Sevilla, Roma and RB Leipzig.

The Clasico triumph at the end of October was particularly significant, cutting Barcelona’s lead at the top of the table and re-energising Madrid’s title challenge.

Los Blancos currently sit third with nine wins from 11 league fixtures and know that another victory would draw them level on points with the Catalan leaders before Barcelona’s next outing.

Rodrygo, Raul Asencio and Ferland Mendy remain unavailable, while Vinicius Junior serves the final match of his domestic suspension.

Even so, Madrid’s squad depth remains formidable. Kylian Mbappe continues to spearhead the attack, Jude Bellingham remains a decisive influence between the lines, and Federico Valverde arrives buoyed by his winning goal against AEK Athens.

Arda Guler and Aurelien Tchouameni are also expected to return to the starting lineup after being rested in Europe.

Valencia should provide a competitive test at Mestalla, particularly after gaining confidence from their recent victory over Elche. The hosts have enough quality to trouble Madrid at times, and home support could help them produce one of their better displays of the season.

However, Real Madrid are operating at a different level right now. Mourinho’s side continue to find ways to win, possess significantly more quality throughout the squad, and are carrying considerable momentum into the fixture.

Valencia may find the net, but Madrid’s attacking strength should ultimately prove decisive.

#1766. Bradley Lowery's mum issues heartbreaking statement to condemn 'cruel' Coventry fan who used her late son's photo to taunt Sunderland fans as 14-year-old boy hands himself into police

Published: 10:02 EDT, 1 November 2026 | Updated: 18:17 EDT, 1 November 2026

Bradley Lowery's mum has released a heartbreaking statement after a Coventry fan appeared to use his photograph to taunt Sunderland supporters.

The deplorable behaviour came during the Premier League clash between the two sides on Saturday, which the Sky Blues won 3-1.

A video on social media showed a supporter holding up a picture of Bradley - who tragically died from a rare form of childhood cancer at the age of six in 2017 - smiling in the direction of Sunderland fans, with the individual pointing at it and seen smirking at the same time.

A 14-year-old boy 'handed himself in' to West Midlands Police on Sunday.

In a statement on Sunday morning after the behaviour of the Coventry fan went viral, Bradley's mum Gemma shared a heartbreaking message.

'My beautiful boy deserves to be remembered with love, not hate,' she wrote. 'Yesterday, a Coventry fan used a photograph of Bradley to taunt Sunderland supporters. As Bradley’s mam, this is heartbreaking, especially as it’s one of my favourite photographs of him. Just look at that smile.

A Coventry fan appeared to use a photograph of Bradley Lowery to taunt Sunderland fans

A fan held up a photo of Bradley, the Sunderland fan who tragically passed away aged six from a rare form of childhood cancer, and was seen smirking and pointing

'I remember that day like it was yesterday. He was so happy, having so much fun. Those moments were precious because they were few and far between. So much of Bradley’s short life was spent battling cancer and enduring treatments no child should ever face. To see such a beautiful memory used in such a cruel way really does make my heart hurt.

'We are a football-loving family who follow Sunderland home and away. I’m all for football banter, but surely mocking a child who died from cancer is not banter? I hope the club takes appropriate action and the young lad’s family help him understand how hurtful his actions were.

'I don’t want hatred directed towards him, so please please don't, just for him to learn from this. Behind that photograph is a little boy who was loved beyond measure and a family who miss him every day. Thank you to everyone who has defended Bradley and shown us so much love. It means more than you know.'

Gemma continued: 'What some people don’t realise is that Bradley’s story didn’t end when his life did. Because of Bradley, children’s lives are being saved, hundreds of families have received vital support, and children facing unimaginable battles are being given hope.

'Through Super Brad’s Pad, families can escape hospital life, spend precious time together and make memories that last forever. That is Bradley’s legacy. The difference my little boy continues to make in this world. No amount of cruelty will ever take that away.

'So rather than let this photograph be remembered for hatred, I want it remembered for what it truly represents. My beautiful little boy, enjoying one of the happiest days of his life, with the biggest smile on his face. That is how I want the world to remember him. #CancerHasNoColours.'

Bradley touched the hearts of football fans across the UK during his battle with neuroblastoma, and formed a touching relationship with then Sunderland striker Jermain Defoe

Confirming that a teenager had handed himself in to authorities on Sunday, West Midlands Police said in a statement: 'We are aware of a video circulating on social media showing an incident at Coventry City's Premier League match with Sunderland.

'A thorough investigation has been launched, and a 14-year-old boy has since handed himself in and will be spoken with in due course.

'We understand the upset and outrage this video has caused in the community and to the victim's family, and our officers are keeping them up to date with the progress of our investigation and working closely alongside both football clubs.'

Coventry condemned the shameful behaviour in a strongly-worded statement on Saturday.

It read: 'Coventry City FC is aware of footage circulating on social media in connection with an incident during our Premier League fixture against Sunderland.

'The club does not tolerate offensive behaviour and will liaise with the relevant authorities to determine the appropriate course of action.'

Since Saturday's clash, more than £1,000 has been donated to the The Bradley Lowery Foundation by Coventry City fans, with many supporters leaving heartfelt messages as they refused to let the actions of one person define them.

Bradley was previously used by a fan as a taunt back in 2023 when Sheffield Wednesday supporter Dale Houghton was seen holding up a picture of him at a match against Sunderland and laughing.

Houghton was subsequently handed a 12-week suspended prison sentence and ordered to do 200 hours unpaid work.

Bradley pictured with his mum Gemma at his sixth birthday party back in May 2017

Bradley touched the hearts of football fans across the UK during his battle with neuroblastoma, a rare form of childhood cancer, before he tragically passed away aged just six in 2017.

The Bradley Lowery Foundation was set up in his honour, with the charity aiming to help families who are fundraising for treatment or equipment that is not readily available or covered by the NHS, while it also supports research into various childhood cancers, including neuroblastoma.

Bradley, who was diagnosed with neuroblastoma when he was just 18 months old, also built up a touching relationship with Jermain Defoe, who later called him his 'best mate'.

Defoe played for Sunderland at the time, and speaking in 2023, he said: 'He will always be in my heart, for the rest of my life. There's not a day that goes past where I don't wake up and think about little Bradley, because his love is genuine.'

#1765. Leeds lineup vs. Tottenham: Predicted XI for Premier League clash

By Oliver Thomas | 05 Nov 2026 16:05, Last updated: 05 Nov 2026 18:28

Leeds United will assess the conditions of four players ahead of Saturday’s Premier League clash with Tottenham Hotspur at Elland Road.

Head coach Daniel Farke has confirmed that Noah Okafor (adductor) and Anton Stach (broken toe) are both major doubts, while he is "carefully optimistic" that star striker Dominic Calvert-Lewin will be fit after missing training on Thursday with a foot problem.

Joe Rodon has missed the last eight games in all competitions with a hamstring injury, but the former Spurs defender is back in full training and in contention to return to the matchday squad.

A start is considered unlikely, though, so a back three of James Justin, Nico Elvedi and Tarik Muharemovic is set to remain intact, while James Trafford will "remain in goal" despite his costly mistake in the 2-0 defeat at Bournemouth last weekend.

Ethan Ampadu and Ao Tanaka will likely link arms again in centre-midfield as Jayden Bogle and Gabriel Gudmundsson operate as wing-backs, the latter of whom is fit having recovered from a knock.

With Leeds struggling to deliver a regular goal threat this season, Farke may be tempted to hand Jean-Matteo Bahoya his first start for the club, with the French attacker having played for just 11 minutes across three substitute appearances since joining in the summer.

Brenden Aaronson is another pushing to start at the expense of either Daniel James or Harry Wilson, while Lukas Nmecha is also hoping to earn a recall and could line up alongside Calvert-Lewin should Farke opt to begin with two focal points in attack.

#1763. Palace’s ill-discipline showed ‘energy and fight’, says Sage

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Pierre Sage had no complaints about the number of yellow cards Crystal Palace were shown against Hoffenheim, highlighting it showed "energy and fight" from his players.

Sage was able to relieve some of the pressure surrounding his position at Selhurst Park with a 1-1 draw against Hoffenheim in the Europa League on Thursday.

The Eagles appeared set for a fourth defeat in five matches in all competitions when Alexander Prass' seventh-minute strike squirmed under the grasp of Dean Henderson.

And in Palace's quest for an equaliser, they thundered into challenges and saw Adam Wharton, Honest Ahanor, Yeremy Pino and Eddie Nketiah all booked in the space of seven minutes, and it got even worse for the hosts 13 minutes from time.

Wharton received his second yellow card for an elbow on Wouter Burger when challenging for the ball in the air. Indeed, no Premier League side have had more red cards in all competitions this season than Palace, with this their third (Manchester United and Sunderland also three).

But Daichi Kamada stepped up with a 91st-minute equaliser for Palace, though Sage does not want regular bookings to become a consistent occurrence for his team.

"For sure, we want to take fewer cards because we need all the players for all the competition," Sage told TNT Sports.

"With the energy and the fight, I think we were in a situation to take the risk of some cards.

"Now we just have to understand that we don't have to be in this situation by managing our game in a better way from the beginning."

On Wharton's red card, the Palace boss added: "I never comment on the decision of the referee. It's difficult to play without him.

"We suffered just after that, but we reorganised ourselves to play with a back four."

A point at Selhurst https://t.co/zDB1eQSDqn

— Crystal Palace F.C. (@CPFC) November 5, 2026

Since losing to AEK Larnaca in their first home match in major European competition, Palace are now unbeaten in their last eight at Selhurst Park (W5 D3).

But they once again struggled in front of goal on Thursday, with Kamada's goal, his fourth in his last 12 games for Palace, the Eagles' first in all competitions on home turf since a 3-1 win over Nottingham Forest on October 11.

Palace generated an expected goals (xG) total of just 1.05 from their 13 attempts, while they also had Henderson to thank for stopping Hoffenheim from going two goals ahead in the first half, with the Eagles captain producing a stunning stop to deny Andrej Kramaric.

"I think it could have been better if we scored before, but I know that Dean Henderson kept us in the game with his saves," Sage added.

"I like the energy of the team and to never give up until the end. This goal came at a good moment. We maybe had a last chance to win the game."

The pressure remains on Sage, though, and things do not get any easier for Palace as Andoni Iraola's Liverpool side make the trip to Selhurst Park this Sunday.

"First of all, recovery and we have to build the gameplan because it's a crazy team with really good players," Sage said of Palace's clash with Liverpool.

"They lost their last two games. I think they will come with a lot of ambition, and we have to deal with that."

#1762. Gasly takes shock Italian GP pole and denies Russell

Sometimes inspiration can come from the unlikeliest of sources. After claiming the first pole of his Formula One career, an absolutely stunning effort in his 192nd attempt – edging out Mercedes’ George Russell right at the death – Alpine’s Pierre Gasly revealed that a harmless jibe from his performance coach Ben Thorpe just before the session started had riled him up.

It turned out Gasly and Russell had been playing online chess until about 15 minutes before qualifying.

“Since the [drivers’] briefing last night, I figured out that he [Russell] is obsessed with chess, and so am I,” Gasly explained later in his press conference. “There are a few of us in the paddock who are. So we have exchanged our IDs on Chess.com and we have had a little game going on.

“I won yesterday, and another one that carried on into today,” the Frenchman added. “I was feeling confident and I was picking [taking] piece after piece. Then Ben told me: ‘You are getting George here but he is going to get you in a few minutes!’. And I thought ‘F--- off!’.”

What a way to break your duck. And what a day on which to do it. On Friday, Gasly lost his only podium of the season when the International Court of Appeal reinstated two five-second penalties he received in Monaco, dropping him from third to seventh in that race. The ruling produced fireworks when Flavio Briatore, Alpine’s executive adviser, then accused one of the judges on the ICA panel of being biased towards McLaren, one of two teams who had brought the appeal.

Another 24 hours later, the fireworks were for all the right reasons. And there was no appealing the result; the start of Russell’s final lap in Q3 was slightly compromised by Red Bull’s Max Verstappen, but the Englishman could have no real complaints, losing out by 0.060secs in the end, prompting wild celebrations in the Alpine garage.

To say the result was a surprise would be an understatement. This was the Enstone team’s first pole in 17 years, since Fernando Alonso took P1 Renault at the 2009 Hungarian Grand Prix.

The warning signs were there. Alpine had been quick all weekend. But the Tifosi packing Monza’s grandstands fully expected it to be a battle between Mercedes and their beloved Ferrari for pole.

The Scuderia’s performance was underwhelming. Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton were only ninth and 10th quickest in Q2, the latter squeaking into Q3 by one thousandth of a second from Audi’s Gabriel Bortoleto. “F--- me,” Hamilton said after dodging that bullet.

And although they improved a bit in Q3, Hamilton managing to claim P5, just behind Leclerc in P4, they never threatened the front row. In fact, they later got lucky as McLaren’s Oscar Piastri, who took P3, was later hit with a three-place grid drop post-qualifying for impeding Liam Lawson, meaning both Ferrari drivers rose one place.

It could prove significant. Hamilton, like Russell, knows this weekend represents a golden opportunity to close the gap to Kimi Antonelli in the title race. The two Britons are tied second in the championship heading into the weekend, 59 points behind the Italian. But Antonelli, who sacrificed his qualifying to help Russell, must start from the back of the grid on Sunday due to exceeding the permitted number of engines in a season.

It promises to be a fascinating race, with Antonelli fighting his way through the pack and Russell and Hamilton trying to make hay while they can. Russell sounded confident. “I think they [Alpine] have got a car that’s got some good straight-line speed, which will be nice for them in the race. But, yeah, confident I’ve got the pace to go for the win.”

Could he be underestimating Gasly again? The Frenchman, who lives locally in Milan and speaks fluent Italian, has won here before. He claimed the only victory of his F1 career at Monza for AlphaTauri in 2020.

“Anything is possible tomorrow,” insisted Steve Nielsen, Alpine’s managing director. “We didn’t expect to be in pole position, we are. Tomorrow, good starts, good strategy, good pit stops – who knows? Let’s try to win it.”

Gasly himself said he had no idea what he was capable of. “My plan is to stay first as long as I can. How long is that going to be? I have no idea. My focus is going to be on my driving and making no mistakes and making the best out of what I have.” Perhaps that will be enough for another checkmate.

Antonelli acknowledged that his engine-parts grid penalty meant he had no reason not to assist his teamate Russell by offering towing assistance.

He seemed a little peeved at times on the radio, but he did his job. With Russell likely to need to return the favour for him later this season, there is no point causing bother.

He told Sky Sports: “It’s what I have to do. The team asked me and of course I did what I had to do, I tried to help as much as possible. It’s a bit weird going in two, even the lap I did alone was a bit of a weird feeling. Overall with the penalty today I had to be a good teammate and I had to help as much as I could. I think I did a good job with that and happy it worked out.”

Here’s Oscar Piastri, asked if a pole had been possible: “I don’t think so, no. I think the first lap felt good and I tried to see if anyone wanted to go in front out of the pit lane but no one did and I knew it was always going to be difficult and misjudged the braking a little bit and locked up. That was the session but good to have a decent result, it has been a while. I’ll take it.”

Alpine managing director Steve Nielsen said to Sky Sports that they were aiming high: “Pierre is a class act, as you say, if you give him the machine, he will deliver. We failed to do that a few times last year. We haven’t always given him the most competitive machinery this year, but when we have he has delivered. Particularly earlier in the season so to see the team bounce back, to see him deliver on the track he knows well, he lives locally, he lives in Milan. It was wonderful.

“We mustn’t forget Franco either, he’s done a great job today. I really feel we have given them a good car, and who knows? Anything is possible tomorrow.”

Here’s what he said immediately after the session: “Massive congrats to Pierre because that’s an incredible performance. We were actually playing a game of chess about 15 minutes before qualifying and he beat me there and I thought ‘well I think I’ll beat you in qualifying’ and here we are - he’s ahead of me again! I was disappointed not to get pole. It was a bit messy with Verstappen opening the lap. But Pierre and Alpine have been super fast, even from Q1. Happy to see them get a good result.”

Gasly’s advantage, it appears, seems to be over Russell’s car understeering and lacking grip in turbulent air.

P1 ☝️#F1 #ItalianGP pic.twitter.com/U0hebWsjWY

He says: “It was amazing, thank you everyone. It was an incredible qualy. I felt very good in the car. I was trying to chip away in evert session. I’m so happy, it’s been nine years trying to get a pole. First win [was] in Monza, to get pole is very special.”

He then pays credit to his team and the fans in Italian, and I am leaning on my Latin to get the gist of it.

“I was disappointed not to get the pole,” admits Russell who said he had been playing chess with Gasly before the game and the Frenchman won that, with Russell confident he was going to beat him in qualifying.

Alpine been in the news all weekend. Fair to say that pole lap from Gasly is better PR for the team than Flavio Briatore’s bizarre outburst in the FIA press conference yesterday. Well done that man.

His tone is evidently disappointed. In truth, given Hamilton is fifth, he is in a strong position to have the best of the weekend.

Gasly, yes, was fastest, but Russell has been the most consistent.

Piastri could be in trouble, too, for impeding earlier in the day’s sesion. Ferrari, in fourth and fifth, do not look entirely competitive.

Russell is second, Piastri third, Leclerc fourth, Hamilton fifth, Verstappen sixth, Antonelli seventh, Colapinto eighth, Norris ninth and Lindblad 10th.

He starts his flying lap, and locks up at turn 1 and exceeds track limits. That means Norris will be unable to get a tow from him too.

After being the quickest at FP2 and FP3, he is top of the pack once more with a bit over five minutes left.

Antonelli has done him a favour there, but Russell may need to return the favour in similar circumstances down the line.

Hamilton is now down in ninth, and struggling, about 0.8s off the pace.

Hamilton needs to catch Leclerc to get a tow. It failed to happen last time out.

Piastri finished Q2 in P2 but it looks likely he'll be penalised for this incident involving Lawson#F1 #ItalianGP pic.twitter.com/RGzzEeqyql

Lawson, Hulkenberg, Sainz, Ocon, Bearman and Bortoleto are all out.

Hamilton is 10th, one-thousandth of a second quick enough to scrape through, and Leclrec ninth.

“**** me” exclaims Hamilton, without saying, ‘Asterisk’ once.

Antonelli asks for the chance to go out with another team ahead so he can get a tow of his own.

Norris now second quickest, so perhaps those brakes are up to speed.

There is some suggestion that Hamilton might need a front wing change.

The Silver Arrows working in tandem Kimi in front, George slipstreaming behind #F1 #ItalianGP pic.twitter.com/H476E91GJs

But Gasly is going fastest in his out lap.

Verstappen now goes fastest. Lawson is in behind, with Carlos Sainz making a surprise appearance up top.

Hamilton and Russell are yet to lay down times.

Norris is uncomfortable with his brakes at Monza.

Given he’s well outside of the fastest for now, the pressure is on him to make Q3.

The two Aston Martins are out, along with Yuki Tsunoda, Alex Albon, Valtteri Bottas and Sergio Perez.

Q2 awaits, with Gasly fastest - aiming for what would be his first pole.

Alonso, meanwhile, has wirthdrawn from the session. Things going wrong for the veteran, who must have no other hobbies.

FOUR MINUTES TO GO IN Q1TOP 6 ⬆️Gasly VerstappenColapintoAntonelliRussellHamiltonBOTTOM 6 ⬇️Hulkenberg AlbonBottasAlonsoStrollPerez#F1 #ItalianGP pic.twitter.com/BYdYjrjtnu

Pierre Gasly takes his Alpine for a spin. He is now fastest, with Verstappen second, and Colapinto bookending the Dutchman.

Antonelli and then Russell next, with the stricken Antonelli likely to give his colleague a tow.

The Red Bull man is 0.216s clear of Hamilton, with Piastri just behind.

No surprising stragglers just yet, but 11 minutes to go of this section.

We’ve 16 minutes left, and some cars are finally coming out to do battle.

18 minutes ahead before the final two rounds. Nobody is doing anything. As they say in football: tactically fascinating.

Monza paddock is absolutely sweltering. 33.8C out here. I just passed Fabio Capello on my way back to the media centre. He was speaking to Sky Sports Italia so I wasn’t able to give him my thoughts on where he went wrong at the 2010 World Cup.

Decent ding dong between Hamilton and Verstappen in practice earlier. Hopefully Hamilton is fired up for this. With Antonelli taking his grid drop at his home race, there’s a big opportunity for both Hamilton and Russell to close the gap this weekend.

The tifosi are ready 🙌It's time for qualifying at the Temple of Speed 👊#F1 #ItalianGP pic.twitter.com/jeiTcb8Ij2

The cars will soon be out on the track, and we’ll have reports of their progress.

There are actually times when affection for a car company makes sense, despite what I said earlier.

Sound on... listen to the reception for Charles and Lewis ❤️#F1 #ItalianGP @ScuderiaFerrari pic.twitter.com/kk6BvA1UdC

As touched on earlier, Lewis Hamilton has to hope Charles Leclerc will work with him.

The Monegasque (look it up) is the junior partner at this point, whether he wants to be or not. That might not make him entirely delighted, but he can tow the British driver around and give him a launch for fast laps, if he’s feeling helpful.

Everyone now has access to PowerPoint, which means we all now have to have, “learnings.”

Imagine if someone you met in real life said that to you.

3 hours of laps and learnings done.#ItalianGP pic.twitter.com/GTvOvL5L5M

Given Antonelli is still one of the quickest on the track, it would be no surprise if he can at least make the top 10.

Favourable accidents and yellow flags might offer up more opportunities, too, but both Hamilton and Russell need to strike while they have such a clear advantage.

George Russell tops Lewis Hamilton in final practice in Monza 🇮🇹💪 pic.twitter.com/jxIO13aRX6

I’m as big a fan of F1 as the next man, assuming the next man quite likes F1, but there is something strange about supporting a car company, isn’t there?

🇮🇹 Sentendo il calore dell'Italia! 🥰🇬🇧 Feeling the warmth of Italy! 🥰 pic.twitter.com/ze6Ww1Z0zx

The session starts in around 40 minutes, so drivers are on their Gameboys and Instagram, and reading the weekend edition of The Telegraph.

Words we live by, this weekend and always ❤️ pic.twitter.com/0QoGlpzOHI

Here’s our interview with Alex Albon about a grim weekend at Monza.

“Alex Albon remembers the 2022 Italian Grand Prix well. He had been looking forward to it. ‘We had a car which was good down the straights that year so I was quite excited to be going to Monza,” the Williams driver recalls, a little wistfully.

‘We did FP1 and FP2 and sure enough we were quick so I was like: ‘This is going to be a good weekend.’

“Albon could not have been more wrong. He remembers waking at around 1am that night and being unable to get back to sleep.

“What happened next was the stuff of nightmares. Albon called the doctor, was diagnosed with appendicitis, sent to San Gerardo Hospital in Monza for surgery, only to suffer an unexpected complication during the procedure, which resulted in acute respiratory failure.”

He shares the joint record with Michael Schumacher for most wins at Monza.

Schumacher, a Ferrari legend, ended his career with five. Hamilton has the same.

Sport loves an emotional link to records, so be prepared for this to become a big moment.

Five wins apiece for Michael and Lewis 🖐#F1 #ItalianGP pic.twitter.com/j10lMygYft

The Italian team are bringing an upgrade engine to Monza for the weekend.

Hamilton would desperately love to go out at the top after what is a remarkable return to decent form after some years of desperate struggle.

With Antonelli possibly out of the running this weekend, this is the chance to change the - *spits in self-scorn* - narrative.

Russell might have incurred a penalty if he had done this in qualifying.

The Mercedes man blocked Oscar Piastri’s run at a corner, forcing some heavy braking from his rival.

Thankfully, Piastri ducked out, and thankfully for Russell, he’s not facing censure.

A near miss for Oscar Piastri! 😬 pic.twitter.com/y6UMu8wIDM

Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton go racing! 🍿 pic.twitter.com/Zs8u8h4XoT

The former world champion is still looking for more from his car.

“Just looking at the deltas there, I was losing something like 0.6secs to George on the straights, which is something we need to look into,” Hamilton said yesterday, before explaining his conundrum for qualifying, suggesting he may go out after Leclerc.

“The tow is everything here so [I’m] likely to be looking for the tow.”

Because Antonelli exceeded the limit of parts used for his engine, he is taking a grid penalty at Monza.

Few would entirely rule out a storming ride for him on Sunday to end up top of the pack, but is is clearly a huge task for him to score points of any kind with that disadvantage.

They are now likely both past their peaks, but Hamilton and Verstappen recalled their battles of 2021 when they clashed in practice earlier.

Verstappen was already hacked off with Hamilton for seemingly obstructing his path earlier in the session, and they almost came together in the dying moments of the session.

Hamilton needed to take the escape road at the first chicane, where the pair made contact in 2021, as Verstappen looked to slip around his occasional rival. The two of them scarcely avoided another contact.

On the radios, Verstappen claimed, “He caused that,” while Hamilton reported to Ferrari that he was, “Blocked by Max.” Perhaps there will be more aggro later.

The full list of times from earlier today.

FP3 CLASSIFICATIONRussell in the box seat heading into qualifying#F1 #ItalianGP pic.twitter.com/BUrCsv92dT

Welcome to Telegraph Sport’s live coverage of and qualifying for the Monza Grand Prix.

Before the weekend’s racing, George Russell was, at least publicly, less than bullish about his chances in Italy.

He did, though, believe he would deliver a better showing than he had in recent weeks.

“I don’t know if we can say we’re favourites this weekend, but we probably have a greater opportunity than we’ve had in the last two races where it’s been less about the power unit and more about the chassis,” he said.

“It’s so close right now, that last tenth in qualifying can be the difference of a couple of positions, which can change the podium. Right now, I don’t know who is going to be the team to beat.”

Russell was almost a minute off winner Lando Norris of McLaren in Hungary, finishing seventh in his Mercedes. Two weeks ago, in the Netherlands, he took the last spot on the podium, with Norris winning again.

However, in the second practice session on Friday and FP3 today, Russell was quickest. He led his former colleague, Ferrari’s Lewis Hamilton, who was second fastest.

Red Bull’s Max Verstappen hinted at a rare good weekend as he was third fastest, about a third of a second behind Russell.

Russell, of course, needs a win soon, or he is in danger of seeing the championship run away from him entirely, as Kimi Antonelli already leads him by 59 points in the world title chase.

Perhaps psychologically just as pressing is that erstwhile teammate Hamilton is tied with Russell on 183 points, in third because he has one victory compared to Russell’s two. Slipping down the rankings could knock his confidence.

Russell has not secured pole for the last four races, so a strong showing in qualifying might be the boost he needs ahead of Sunday’s race, while Norris is looking for a pole position hat-trick.

#1760. Former Liverpool defender Stephen Warnock reveals he hid seizures from club because he was 'petrified' of being released as youngster

Published: 19:09 EDT, 1 November 2026 | Updated: 19:15 EDT, 1 November 2026

Former Liverpool defender Stephen Warnock has revealed he hid seizures from the club out of fear that the Reds would axe him.

Warnock, 44, played 67 times for Liverpool and has transitioned into broadcasting since retiring from playing in 2018.

He suffered from a number of epileptic fits as a youngster - a condition that affects around one in every 100 people.

Warnock never understood what was causing his seizures and told 5 Live: 'I was petrified of telling Liverpool because I was worried about being released. Because I was thinking "if they think I've got a condition they will release me".

'I was worried about being on the pitch and it happens. There were no triggers for me, I never knew what triggered it. That was what petrified me.'

Warnock experienced the seizures for around three years and underwent a number of tests including a CT and MRI scan.

Stephen Warnock, pictured working as a broadcaster, revealed he suffered from seizures

The former Liverpool defender, pictured in action for the Reds back in 2005, said he was terrified of telling the club about his health issue

'I was at a computer and then I woke up in a hospital bed,' he went on. 'And I was like "wow, how have I got here?". I didn't remember anything, I completely blacked out.

'My friends told me I started having a seizure. Obviously an ambulance was called and I was taken to a hospital bed.

'I was embarrassed to be honest, because no-one else had it, no-one knew about it, I didn't know about it until it happened.'

The risk of having a seizure can be reduced with medication and Warnock has not experienced one since he was 14.

'I was in a fortunate position where I grew out of it,' he said.

'I didn't have to go on medication or worry about driving a car or things like that. It's the first time I've ever really spoken about it.'

Warnock, a left-back, departed Liverpool in 2007 and went on to play for Aston Villa, Leeds and Derby among other sides.

He has appeared on a number of television channels while working as a pundit, including the BBC, Sky Sports, BT Sport, NBC and DAZN.

#1759. Newport County vs Walsall - prediction, team news, lineups

By Darren Plant | 05 Nov 2026 16:11

Newport County and Walsall square off in the FA Cup first round on Saturday afternoon.

These two teams play in the fourth tier of English football, sitting in 14th and third position in the League Two table respectively.

Having signed a long-term contract with Walsall, Lee Grant will get time to secure promotion to League One.

However, the Saddlers entered November having lost just one of 13 games in League Two, that defeat coming by a 4-2 scoreline to runaway leaders Salford City.

Walsall have conceded just eight goals in their other 12 league games, while they bounced back from the Salford disappointment by beating Colchester United last time out.

Sitting in third place with a game in hand on the teams below them, Grant will be delighted with the progression of his team.

Only once in eight years - the 2020-21 coronavirus-hit campaign - have Walsall failed to reach the second round of the FA Cup.

Just as impressively, Newport have only not progressed to the second round of the competition on two occasions in 11 years.

After consecutive near-misses with relegation to the National League, Newport have 18 points from their opening 14 games in 2026-27.

Hayden Mullins has brought some much-needed stability to the club, losing just four times across the aforementioned period.

Although Walsall are yet to suffer a league away defeat, Newport have not lost in seven League Two fixtures at Rodney Parade.

This tie was drawn out in the first round of the 2016-17 FA Cup, Newport prevailing by a 2-1 scoreline on that occasion.

Having been able to make changes in the EFL Trophy in midweek, Mullins may stick with a similar Newport XI from the 4-1 win over Chesterfield last weekend.

Harrison Biggins played a key role with a goal and an assist, taking him to seven such contributions in League Two during 2026-27.

Shaquille Gwengwe is available again after serving a three-match ban for an incident in the fixture with York City on October 17.

Ryan Leak, James Furlong, Sven Sprangler, Courtney Clarke and Andy Dallas could all return to the Walsall XI, with Grant likely to want to freshen up his team.

Declan Skura, Mason Hancock, Isaac Moore, Reece Smith and Aaron Pressley - five players who have accumulated a lot of game time in League Two - could drop down to the substitutes' bench.

#1758. ‘Winning mentality becomes contagious’ – Adams revels in Bournemouth’s stellar run

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Tyler Adams believes "winning mentality becomes contagious" after Bournemouth secured their seventh consecutive victory with a win over Sparta Prague in the Europa League.

Adams, Evanilson and Rayan all came off the bench as the Cherries came back from a goal down to defeat Sparta 3-1 at epet ARENA.

The home side took the lead through Ebrima Singhateh, but a first-half red card for Tobias Guddal let Bournemouth back into the contest.

Bournemouth have won seven consecutive matches in all competitions for the first time since November 2014, when they were playing in England's second tier.

They are one of three sides in the Europa League still with a 100% record after four games, along with Benfica and Ferencvaros, with the Cherries second in the table.

Adams scored his second goal in major European competition and his first in 20 such appearances, since netting for RB Leipzig against Atletico Madrid in the Champions League in August 2020, but he has warned his team-mates not to become complacent.

"Can’t get too comfortable," the Bournemouth midfielder told TNT Sports.

"You have to be able to hold that winning standard, that winning mentality becomes contagious especially when you are playing every three days.

"It doesn’t feel that long ago since we lost 5-1 to Chelsea and that stings a little bit, we don’t want to feel that ever again.

"I think we turned a page and we have been a more mature team ever since that; the way that we defend, the way that we take pride in the mentality of making sure we don’t give the opposition any opportunity to breathe.

"Everyone is working hard every day in training, guys that aren't playing are working hard, the guys that are playing are working hard so there's a lot of competition but that breathes success. I'm happy with the team's performance."

A journalist has claimed that AC Milan want to sign Alejandro Balde from Barcelona, but they face strong competition to get him.

Going into the January window, there continues to be talk about Milan strengthening in the left wing-back role. Pervis Estupinan has not been convincing since his arrival, and Davide Bartesaghi is now being used even further forward, as is Diego Moreira.

He adds that both Andoni Iraola and Rúben Amorim ‘are fans of the player and believe he would fit perfectly into their respective systems’. Barcelona are not opposed to a sale but are asking for a minimum of €45m to let him go.

#1756. Next Man Utd manager: Red Devils make Didier Deschamps 'move' amid Michael Carrick sack talk

By Carter White | 05 Nov 2026 16:25, Last updated: 05 Nov 2026 20:48

Manchester United have reportedly made contact with Didier Deschamps over potentially taking charge from Michael Carrick as head coach.

The former Red Devils midfielder is under extreme pressure at Old Trafford following an awful domestic start to the campaign, with the 20-time English champions currently sitting in 17th spot in the Premier League table.

Despite being level on points with the top-flight relegation zone after nine matches, Man Utd produced a marvellous comeback on the continental scene earlier in the week, beating Italian giants Roma 3-2 at the Theatre of Dreams.

The Red Devils have been heavily linked to Europa League specialist Unai Emery in recent weeks, however, Aston Villa are supposedly closing in on a contract agreement for the Spaniard.

One of the top-performing bosses in European football at the moment, Cesc Fabregas of Como recently masterminded a 9-1 battering of Lens in the League Phase of the Champions League on Wednesday night.

According to French publication Footmercato, Manchester United have added another high-profile name to their shortlist of possible managerial replacements for Carrick, who is walking on thin ice at Old Trafford.

The Red Devils have supposedly made initial contact with former France manager Deschamps, who has been out of work since taking Les Bleus to the semi-finals of the 2026 World Cup in North America.

The report states that the 58-year-old is not particularly keen on a switch to the Theatre of Dreams given the club's current predicament, however, a deal between the two parties cannot be ruled out.

It is understood that Man Utd have also touched base with Aston Villa hero Emery and ex-Germany and Bayern Munich head coach Julian Nagelsmann, with Carrick potentially one poor result away from the sack.

After departing his French post in July, it is believed that Deschamps was under consideration for the vacant position at Real Madrid before Los Blancos decided to reunite with Jose Mourinho.

To a certain extent, Didier Deschamps was the final evolution of Gareth Southgate on the international scene, receiving plenty of criticism during his long reign but ultimately lifting titles - something that his English counterpart failed to do.

The 58-year-old managed superstars such as Paul Pogba, N'Golo Kante, Olivier Giroud and Kylian Mbappe to success at the 2018 World Cup in Russia, where Luka Modric's Croatia were beaten in the final.

After that, a 2021 UEFA Nations League title did little to address the clamour for further major trophies in France, with Deschamps's side failing to lift the 2026 World Cup despite possessing arguably the best starting XI at the tournament.

#1755. Celtic victory over Besiktas reminded O’Neill ‘of the olden days’

Syndicated reporting provided by Stats Perform and reviewed by the SoccerNews editorial team.

Martin O'Neill was reminded "of the olden days" after Celtic fans roared their side on to a Europa League victory over Besiktas.

Camilo Duran scored twice off the bench as Celtic defeated Besiktas 3-2 at home on Thursday, with 20-year-old Callum Osmand also getting on the scoresheet for the hosts.

Besiktas took the lead through Junior Olaitan, who scored the rebound off his own penalty miss, and Orkun Kokcu restored parity in the 85th minute after goals from Osmand and Duran.

But Duran had the final say two minutes later, clinching Celtic's first win in the Europa League this season.

Duran became the first substitute to score two goals in a major European competition for Celtic since Johannes Edvaldsson against Jeunesse d'Esch in the European Cup in September 1977.

Celtic’s victory ended a run of three successive defeats at home in the Europa League, since their last such win in January against Utrecht (4-2), and O'Neill took great delight in their home support.

"The crowd gives us something and tonight was particularly special. It reminded me of the olden days," the Celtic boss told TNT Sports.

+! #CelticBeşiktaş | #UEL | #CelticFC https://t.co/sPnWuZJxs1

— Celtic Football Club (@CelticFC) November 5, 2026

"A really good performance. Hearts and soul into the game. Just when I thought we were going to drop two points, we came back again. So much spirit.

"It's been tough in Europe, tonight was tough. We always still think about trying to qualify – at least we've given ourselves a chance.

"We made some changes, freshened things up. We have to give the opportunity [to players] because we play a lot of games in quick succession."

Celtic are the second team to win a Europa League match this season having conceded the opening goal in the second half, after Celta Vigo, who did so against Celtic on matchday three (2-1).

Aged 20 years 362 days, Osmand is the youngest player to score in major European competition for Celtic since Liel Abada (20 yrs 32d) in November 2021, against Ferencvaros in the Europa League.
